title.en: Volume 65 Biographies 30: Zhou Luohou, Zhou Fashang, Li Jing, Murong Sancang, Xue Shixiong, Wang Rengong, Quan Wu, Tu Wanxu, Dong Chun, Zhao Cai
title.raw: 卷65 列傳第30 周羅睺 周法尚 李景 慕容三藏 薛世雄 王仁恭 權武 吐萬緒 董純 趙才 Volume 65 Biographies 30: Zhou Luohou, Zhou Fashang, Li Jing, Murong Sancang, Xue Shixiong, Wang Rengong, Quan Wu, Tu Wanxu, Dong Chun, Zhao Cai

sentences.zh: 周羅睺

translations.literal: Zhou Luohou
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Luohou

sentences.zh: 周羅睺，字公佈，九江尋陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Luohou, styled Gongbu, was a native of Xunyang in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Luohou, whose courtesy name was Gongbu, came from Xunyang in Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父法暠，仕梁冠軍將軍、始興太守、通直散騎常侍、南康內史，臨蒸縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Fagao served Liang as General Who Champions the Army, Administrator of Shixing, Regular Attendant for Direct Communication at Court, Internal Secretary of Nankang, and Marquis of Linzheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fagao had served Liang as Champion General, Administrator of Shixing, Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, Internal Secretary of Nankang, and Marquis of Linzheng.

sentences.zh: 羅睺年十五，善騎射，好鷹狗，任俠放蕩，收聚亡命，陰習兵書。

translations.literal: At age fifteen Luohou was skilled in mounted archery, fond of hawks and hunting dogs, unrestrained and chivalrous, gathered fugitives, and privately studied books of war.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he was an expert horseman and archer who loved hawking and hunting dogs; he lived as a swaggering knight-errant, gathered outlaws about him, and studied military texts in secret.

sentences.zh: 從祖景彥誡之曰：「吾世恭謹，汝獨放縱，難以保家。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Jing Yan admonished him, saying: "Our family for generations has been respectful and cautious; you alone are unrestrained. It will be hard to preserve the household."
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Jing Yan warned him: "Our line has always been dutiful and careful, yet you alone run wild. You will be hard put to keep the family intact."

sentences.zh: 若不喪身，必將滅吾族。

translations.literal: If you do not lose your life, you will surely bring ruin upon our clan.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not lose your own life, you will surely destroy our whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」羅睺終不改。

translations.literal: Luohou in the end did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou never changed his ways.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝時，以軍功授開遠將軍、句容令。

translations.literal: During the time of Chen Emperor Xuan, for military merit he was appointed General Who Opens the Distance and Magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Chen he was rewarded for military service with the post of General Who Opens the Distance and Magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 後從大都督吳明徹與齊師戰于江陽，為流矢中其左目。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Commander-in-Chief Wu Mingche in battle with the Qi army at Jiangyang and was struck in his left eye by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the commander-in-chief Wu Mingche against the Qi army at Jiangyang and was hit in the left eye by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 齊師圍明徹於宿預也，諸軍相顧，莫有鬥心。

translations.literal: When the Qi army besieged Mingche at Suyu, the various armies looked at one another and none had the will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi forces besieged Mingche at Suyu, the allied armies exchanged uneasy glances and none dared to fight.

sentences.zh: 羅睺躍馬突進，莫不披靡。

translations.literal: Luohou leaped on his horse and charged forward; none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou spurred his horse straight into the enemy line, and nothing could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 太僕卿蕭摩訶因而副之，斬獲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Husbandry Xiao Mohe thereupon supported him, and kills and captures were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Husbandry Xiao Mohe then joined the attack, and the slaughter and captures were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 進師徐州，與周將梁士彥戰于彭城，摩訶臨陣墜馬，羅睺進救，拔摩訶於重圍之內，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Advancing the army to Xuzhou, they fought with the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Pengcheng; Mohe fell from his horse in battle, and Luohou advanced to rescue him, pulling Mohe out from within the heavy encirclement—his bravery was foremost in the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the army advanced on Xuzhou and fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Pengcheng, Mohe was unhorsed in the press of battle; Luohou charged in, dragged him from the thick of the encirclement, and his courage ranked first in all three armies.

sentences.zh: 明徹之敗也，羅睺全眾而歸，拜光遠將軍、鐘離太守。

translations.literal: When Mingche was defeated, Luohou brought the whole force back safely and was appointed General of Expansive Light and Administrator of Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingche's defeat, Luohou brought the entire force back intact and was appointed General of Expansive Light and Administrator of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授使持節、都督霍州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Huo province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he received the staff of authority and was made commander of all military affairs in Huo province.

sentences.zh: 平山賊十二洞，除右軍將軍、始安縣伯，邑四百戶，總管檢校揚州內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandits of the twelve caves on Ping Mountain, was appointed General of the Right Army and Baron of Shian county with a fief of four hundred households, and served as Commander-in-Chief inspecting all military affairs inside and outside Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the mountain bandits of the twelve cave strongholds, was made General of the Right Army and Baron of Shian with a fief of four hundred households, and was put in overall charge of military affairs within and beyond Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賜金銀三千兩，盡散之將士，分賞驍雄。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand taels of gold and silver and distributed it all to the officers and men, dividing it to reward the bravest.
translations.idiomatic: He was given three thousand taels of gold and silver, distributed the whole sum among his officers and men, and shared it out to reward the bravest fighters.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝深歎美之。

translations.literal: Chen Emperor Xuan deeply sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen sighed deeply in admiration.

sentences.zh: 出為晉陵太守，進爵為侯，增封一千戶。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jinling, was advanced in rank to Marquis, and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Jinling, advanced to marquis, and his fief was increased by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除太僕卿，增封並前一千六百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Minister of Husbandry, and his fief was increased so that together with before it was one thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Minister of Husbandry, and his fief, including previous grants, was raised to sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋除雄信將軍，使持節、都督豫章十郡諸軍事、豫章內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of Majestic Trust, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the ten commanderies of Yuzhang, and Internal Secretary of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of Majestic Trust, bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in the ten commanderies of Yuzhang, and Internal Secretary of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 獄訟庭決，不關吏手，民懷其惠，立碑頌德焉。

translations.literal: In prison cases and lawsuits he decided at court without relying on clerks' hands; the people cherished his kindness and set up a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He judged lawsuits in open court without leaving matters to clerks; the people cherished his kindness and erected a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 至德中，除持節，都督南川諸軍事。

translations.literal: During the Zhade period he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the Southern Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhade era he was given the staff of authority and made commander of all military affairs in the Southern Pass.

sentences.zh: 江州司馬吳世興密奏羅睺甚得人心，擁眾嶺表，意在難測，陳主惑焉。

translations.literal: The Jiangzhou Assistant Commander Wu Shixing secretly memorialized that Luohou had won people's hearts greatly, held troops beyond the passes, and his intentions were hard to fathom—the Chen ruler was perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shixing, assistant commander of Jiangzhou, secretly reported that Luohou had won extraordinary loyalty, held troops south of the passes, and might harbor designs that were hard to read; the Chen ruler was troubled.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶、魯廣達等保明之。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe, Lu Guangda, and others spoke clearly in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe, Lu Guangda, and others vouched for him and cleared his name.

sentences.zh: 外有知者，或勸其反，羅睺拒絕之。

translations.literal: Among outsiders who knew of it, some urged him to rebel; Luohou refused.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who knew him from outside, some urged him to rebel, but Luohou refused.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除太子左衛率，信任逾重，時參宴席。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent; trust in him grew heavier, and at times he joined banquets.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the court trusted him ever more deeply, and he was often invited to banquets.

sentences.zh: 陳主曰：「周左率武將，詩每前成，文士何為後也？

translations.literal: The Chen ruler said: "The military man Zhou the Left Guardian completes his poems first every time—why do the literati come after?"
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler said: "Commander Zhou is a fighting man, yet his poems are always finished first—why do the literati lag behind?"

sentences.zh: 」都官尚書孔范對曰：「周羅睺執筆制詩，還如上馬入陣，不在人後。

translations.literal: The Minister of Revenue Kong Fan replied: "When Zhou Luohou takes brush to compose poetry, it is still like mounting a horse and entering battle—he is not behind others."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Kong Fan replied: "When Zhou Luohou takes up the brush to compose verse, it is like mounting a horse and charging into battle—he is never behind anyone."

sentences.zh: 」自是益見親禮。

translations.literal: From this he was even more seen with intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was treated with still greater intimacy and honor.

sentences.zh: 出督湘州諸軍事，還拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He went out as commander of all military affairs of Xiang province and on return was appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to command military affairs in Xiang province and, on his return, was appointed Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣之伐陳也，都督巴峽緣江諸軍事，以拒秦王俊，軍不得渡，相持逾月。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang attacked Chen, he was commander of all military affairs along the Ba gorges and the Yangzi, to resist Qin Prince Jun; the armies could not cross and faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang marched against Chen, Luohou commanded all forces along the Ba gorges and the Yangzi to block Qin Prince Jun; neither army could cross, and they faced each other for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 遇丹陽陷，陳主被擒，上江猶不下，晉王廣遣陳主手書命之，羅睺與諸將大臨三日，放兵士散，然後乃降。

translations.literal: When Danyang fell and the Chen ruler was captured, the upper Yangzi still would not submit; Prince Jin Guang sent the Chen ruler's own handwritten order, and Luohou with the generals wept greatly for three days, released the troops to disperse, and only then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Danyang fell and the Chen ruler was taken, the upper Yangzi still held out; Prince Jin Guang sent the captive ruler's own handwritten command, and Luohou and his generals mourned openly for three days, dismissed the troops, and only then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 高祖慰諭之，許以富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu comforted and instructed him, promising him wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu comforted him and promised him wealth and high office.

sentences.zh: 羅睺垂泣而對曰：「臣荷陳氏厚遇，本朝淪亡，無節可紀。

translations.literal: Luohou wept and replied: "Your servant received thick favor from the Chen; when that dynasty fell I had no constancy to record."
translations.idiomatic: Luohou answered through his tears: "Your servant received great kindness from the house of Chen; when that dynasty fell I had no loyal deed worth recording."

sentences.zh: 陛下所賜，獲全為幸，富貴榮祿，非臣所望。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty bestows—merely to be spared is fortune; wealth, glory, salary, and rank are not what your servant desires.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Your Majesty grants me, merely to be spared is fortune enough; wealth, glory, salary, and rank are not what I seek.

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚器之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu thought very highly of him.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼謂之曰：「聞公郢、漢捉兵，即知揚州可得。

translations.literal: He Ruo said to him: "Hearing that you held troops at Ying and Han, I knew at once that Yangzhou could be taken."
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo said to him: "When I heard that you were holding troops at Ying and Han, I knew at once that Yangzhou could be taken."

sentences.zh: 王師利涉，果如所量。

translations.literal: When the royal army crossed the river with advantage, it was indeed as measured.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army crossed the river with ease, events proved exactly as I had judged.

sentences.zh: 」羅睺答曰：「若得與公周旋，勝負未可知也。

translations.literal: Luohou replied: "Had I been able to contend with you, victory and defeat would be uncertain."
translations.idiomatic: Luohou replied: "Had I been able to meet you in battle, the outcome would still have been uncertain."

sentences.zh: 」其年秋，拜上儀同三司，鼓吹羽儀，送之於宅。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed Senior Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, with drums and feathered banners escorting him to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed Senior Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and drums and feathered banners escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳裨將羊翔歸降於我，使為鄉導，位至上開府，班在羅睺上。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Chen deputy general Yang Xiang had surrendered to us and was made guide, reaching Upper Opener of the Government rank, his court order standing above Luohou's.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Chen deputy general Yang Xiang had surrendered and served as guide; he rose to Upper Opener of the Government, ranking above Luohou at court.

sentences.zh: 韓擒於朝堂戲之曰：「不知機變，立在羊翔之下，能無愧乎？

translations.literal: Han Qin jested with him at court: "Not knowing when to turn—standing below Yang Xiang—can you not feel shame?"
translations.idiomatic: At court Han Qin teased him: "You did not know when to turn with the times, yet you stand below Yang Xiang—can you feel no shame?"

sentences.zh: 」羅睺答曰：「昔在江南，久承令問，謂公天下節士。

translations.literal: Luohou replied: "Formerly in Jiangnan I long received your fine reputation and took you for the empire's man of integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Luohou replied: "Long ago in the south I had heard your fine reputation and took you for the empire's man of integrity."

sentences.zh: 今日所言，殊匪誠臣之論。

translations.literal: What you say today is utterly unlike the talk of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: What you say today is nothing like the speech of a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 」擒有愧色。

translations.literal: Qin flushed with shame.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qin flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，除豳州刺史，俄轉涇州刺史，母憂去職。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Administrator of Bin province; soon transferred to Administrator of Jing province; left office on mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made Administrator of Bin province, soon transferred to Jing province, and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 未期，復起，授豳州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: Before the term was up he was recalled, appointed Administrator of Bin province again, and in both posts had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning term was finished he was recalled and again made Administrator of Bin; in both posts he won a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起遼東之役，徵為水軍總管。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the eastern campaign to Liaodong was launched; he was summoned as Commander-in-Chief of the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Liaodong campaign was launched, he was summoned as commander of the naval forces.

sentences.zh: 自東萊泛海，趣平壤城，遭風，船多飄沒，無功而還。

translations.literal: From Donglai he went by sea toward Pyongyang; encountering wind, many ships drifted and were lost, and he returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed from Donglai toward Pyongyang, met fierce winds, lost many ships, and returned without success.

sentences.zh: 十九年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，從楊素擊之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Türk Qaghan Tardu invaded the frontier; he followed Yang Su in striking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when the Türk qaghan Tardu raided the frontier, he followed Yang Su against them.

sentences.zh: 虜眾甚盛，羅睺白素曰：「賊陣未整，請擊之。

translations.literal: The enemy force was very great; Luohou said to Su: "The bandit array is not yet formed—please let me attack."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy host was very large; Luohou told Su: "Their formation is not yet set—let me strike them."

sentences.zh: 」素許焉，與輕勇二十騎直沖虜陣，從申至酉，短兵屢接，大破之。

translations.literal: Su assented; with twenty picked light horsemen he charged straight into the enemy array; from shen to you they repeatedly closed in hand-to-hand and thoroughly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed; with twenty picked light horsemen he charged straight into the enemy line and, from mid-afternoon until evening, fought hand to hand again and again until the foe was thoroughly broken.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Great General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Great General.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，為東宮右虞候率，賜爵義寧郡公，食邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou he was Eastern Palace Right Commandant of the Household Guards, enfeoffed as Duke of Yining commandery with a fief of 1,500 households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou he became Right Commandant of the Eastern Palace Household Guards, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yining commandery, and received a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 俄轉右衛率。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Right Commandant of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Right Commandant of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was appointed Great General of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was appointed Great General of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，詔副楊素討平之，進授上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, an edict made him deputy to Yang Su to suppress and pacify them; he was advanced to Senior Great General.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, an edict made him Yang Su's deputy to suppress the revolt, and he was advanced to Senior Great General.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，帝幸洛陽。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor visited Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 陳主卒，羅睺請一臨哭，帝許之。

translations.literal: When the former Chen ruler died, Luohou requested to go once to mourn; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the former Chen ruler died, Luohou asked leave to go and mourn him once, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 縗絰送至墓所，葬還，釋服而後入朝。

translations.literal: In hemp mourning garb he escorted to the tomb; after burial he doffed the garb and only then attended court.
translations.idiomatic: He went in hemp mourning garb to escort the body to the tomb; after the burial he put off mourning dress and only then returned to court.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉尚，世論稱其有禮。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this; public opinion called him scrupulous in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised this conduct, and public opinion called him a man of proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 時諒餘党據晉、絳等三州未下，詔羅睺行絳、晉、呂三州諸軍事，進兵圍之。

translations.literal: At that time Liang's remaining parties held Jin, Jiang, and other three prefectures and had not submitted; an edict made Luohou commander of military affairs of Jiang, Jin, and Lü, and he advanced to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang's remaining followers still held Jin, Jiang, and other prefectures; an edict put Luohou in command of military affairs in Jiang, Jin, and Lü, and he advanced to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 為流矢所中，卒于師，時年六十四。

translations.literal: He was struck by a stray arrow and died in the army, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck by a stray arrow and died in the field at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 送柩還京，行數里，無故輿馬自止，策之不動，有飄風旋繞焉。

translations.literal: When the bier was sent back to the capital, after several li for no reason the carriage and horses stopped on their own; whipping them they would not move, and a swirling wind circled about.
translations.idiomatic: As the bier was being sent back to the capital, after a few li the carriage and horses for no apparent reason halted of themselves; though whipped, they would not move, and a swirling wind circled about them.

sentences.zh: 絳州長史郭雅稽顙咒曰：「公恨小寇未平邪？

translations.literal: Jiang prefecture Chief Administrator Guo Ya kowtowed and prayed: "Does Your Lordship resent that the petty bandits are not yet pacified?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ya, chief administrator of Jiang prefecture, kowtowed and prayed: "Does my lord resent that the petty bandits are not yet destroyed?"

sentences.zh: 尋即除殄，無為戀恨。

translations.literal: They will soon be wiped out—do not linger in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They will soon be wiped out—do not linger in resentment.

sentences.zh: 」於是風靜馬行，見者莫不悲歎。

translations.literal: Thereupon the wind stilled and the horses went; all who saw it none did not sigh in grief.
translations.idiomatic: At that the wind died down and the horses moved on; all who witnessed it sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 其年秋七月，子仲隱夢見羅睺曰：「我明日當戰。

translations.literal: That autumn in the seventh month his son Zhongyin dreamed Luohou said: "Tomorrow I shall fight."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month, his son Zhongyin dreamed that Luohou said: "Tomorrow I shall fight."

sentences.zh: 」其靈坐所有弓箭刀劍，無故自動，若人帶持之狀。

translations.literal: At his spirit seat the bows, arrows, swords, and blades for no reason moved on their own as if a person were wearing and holding them.
translations.idiomatic: At his spirit seat the bows, arrows, swords, and blades moved of themselves for no reason, as though a man were buckling them on and taking them up.

sentences.zh: 絳州城陷，是其日也。

translations.literal: Jiang prefecture city fell—that was the very day.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang prefecture city fell on that very day.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國、右翊衛大將軍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Pillar of State and Great General of the Right Wing Guards, posthumous name Zhuang (Stalwart).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Pillar of State and Great General of the Right Wing Guards, with the posthumous name Zhuang (Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 贈物千段。

translations.literal: A thousand bundles of goods were granted in mourning gifts.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand bundles of goods were granted as mourning gifts.

sentences.zh: 子仲安，官至上開府。

translations.literal: His son Zhong'an rose to Upper Opener of the Government.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong'an rose to the rank of Upper Opener of the Government.

sentences.zh: 周法尚

translations.literal: Zhou Fashang
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fashang

sentences.zh: 周法尚，字德邁，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fashang, styled Demai, was a native of Ancheng in Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fashang, whose courtesy name was Demai, came from Ancheng in Ruyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖靈起，梁直閤將軍、義陽太守、廬桂二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingqi was Liang Direct Attendant at the Gate, Administrator of Yiyang, and Inspector of the two provinces Lu and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingqi had been Liang Direct Attendant at the Gate, Administrator of Yiyang, and Inspector of Lu and Gui provinces.

sentences.zh: 父炅，定州刺史、平北將軍。

translations.literal: His father Jiong was Administrator of Dingzhou and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiong had been Administrator of Dingzhou and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 法尚少果勁有風概，好讀兵書。

translations.literal: Fashang in youth was resolute and forceful with spirit, fond of reading military books.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fashang was resolute and spirited, and loved to read books of war.

sentences.zh: 年十八，為陳始興王中兵參軍，尋加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was Central Army Major attached to the Prince of Shixing of Chen, and soon added General Who Subdues Waves.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he became Central Army Major on the staff of Chen's Prince of Shixing, and was soon given the additional title General Who Subdues Waves.

sentences.zh: 其父卒後，監定州事，督父本兵。

translations.literal: After his father's death he supervised affairs of Dingzhou and commanded his father's original troops.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he supervised Dingzhou affairs and took command of his father's former troops.

sentences.zh: 數有戰功，遷使持節、貞毅將軍、散騎常侍，領齊昌郡事，封山陰縣侯，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly had battle merit and was promoted to Bearer of the Staff, General of Steadfast Resolution, Regular Attendant, in charge of Qichang commandery affairs, enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyin county with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories in battle he was promoted to bearer of the staff, General of Steadfast Resolution, and Regular Attendant, placed in charge of Qichang commandery, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyin with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以其兄武昌縣公法僧代為定州刺史。

translations.literal: His elder brother the Duke of Wuchang county Faseng was made Administrator of Dingzhou in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Faseng, Duke of Wuchang county, was made Administrator of Dingzhou in his place.

sentences.zh: 法尚與長沙王叔堅不相能，叔堅言其將反。

translations.literal: Fashang and the Prince of Changsha Shujian were incompatible; Shujian said he was about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang and the Prince of Changsha, Shujian, were on bad terms; Shujian reported that he was about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝執禁法僧，發兵欲取法尚。

translations.literal: Chen Emperor Xuan arrested and imprisoned Faseng and sent troops intending to take Fashang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen arrested and imprisoned Faseng and sent troops to seize Fashang.

sentences.zh: 其下將吏皆勸之歸北，法尚猶豫未決。

translations.literal: His subordinate officers all urged him to go north; Fashang hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all urged him to go over to the north, but Fashang hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 長史殷文則曰：「樂毅所以辭燕，良由不猶已。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yin Wence said: "The reason Yue Yi left Yan was simply because they did not trust him."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yin Wence said: "Yue Yi left Yan for no other reason than that they no longer trusted him."

sentences.zh: 事勢如此，請早裁之。

translations.literal: The situation being thus, please decide soon.
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand as they do now—please decide quickly.

sentences.zh: 」法尚遂歸於周。

translations.literal: Fashang thereupon went over to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang thereupon went over to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 宣帝甚優寵之，拜開府、順州刺史，封歸義縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan greatly favored and cherished him, appointed Opener of the Government, Administrator of Shunzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyi county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan treated him with great favor, appointed him Opener of the Government and Administrator of Shunzhou, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Guiyi county with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 賜良馬五匹，女妓五人，彩物五百段，加以金帶。

translations.literal: He was granted five fine horses, five female entertainers, five hundred bundles of colored goods, and in addition a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was given five fine horses, five female entertainers, five hundred bundles of colored goods, and a gold belt besides.

sentences.zh: 陳將樊猛濟江討之，法尚遣部曲督韓明詐為背己，奔于陳，偽告猛曰：「法尚部兵不願降北，人皆竊議，盡欲叛還。

translations.literal: The Chen general Fan Meng crossed the Yangzi to attack him; Fashang sent his subordinate Commander Han Ming feigning to turn against him and flee to Chen, falsely telling Meng: "Fashang's troops do not wish to go north to surrender; men all whisper in private and all wish to rebel and return."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen general Fan Meng crossed the Yangzi to attack him; Fashang sent his subordinate commander Han Ming, who pretended to turn against him and fled to Chen, falsely telling Meng: "Fashang's troops do not wish to surrender to the north; they whisper among themselves and all want to rebel and return."

sentences.zh: 若得軍來，必無鬥者，自當於陣倒戈耳。

translations.literal: If troops come they surely will not fight—on their own they will turn their blades in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: If your army comes, they will surely not fight; they will turn their blades in the ranks of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 」猛以為然，引師急進。

translations.literal: Meng believed it and led his army in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Meng believed him and hurried his army forward.

sentences.zh: 法尚乃陽為畏懼，自保于江曲。

translations.literal: Fashang thereupon feigned fear and defended himself at the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang then feigned fear and held himself on the defensive at the river bend.

sentences.zh: 猛陳兵挑戰，法尚先伏輕舸於浦中，又伏精銳于古村之北，自張旗幟，迎流拒之。

translations.literal: Meng arrayed troops and challenged battle; Fashang first hid light boats in the harbor and elite troops north of Gucun village, himself raising banners and flags to meet the current and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Meng drew up his troops and offered battle; Fashang had already hidden light boats in the harbor and elite troops north of Gucun village, and himself raised banners and flags to meet the current and resist.

sentences.zh: 戰數合，偽退登岸，投古村，猛舍舟逐之，法尚又疾走。

translations.literal: After several bouts he feigned retreat, went ashore, and threw himself into Gucun; Meng abandoned boats and pursued him, and Fashang ran fast again.
translations.idiomatic: After several clashes he feigned retreat, went ashore, and made for Gucun; Meng abandoned his boats and pursued, and Fashang fled swiftly again.

sentences.zh: 行數里，與村北軍合，復前擊猛。

translations.literal: After several li he joined the army north of the village and again advanced to strike Meng.
translations.idiomatic: After several li he joined the troops north of the village and turned to strike Meng again.

sentences.zh: 猛退走赴船，既而浦中伏舸取其舟楫，建周旗幟。

translations.literal: Meng retreated running to the boats, and soon the hidden boats in the harbor took his vessels and paddles and raised Zhou banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Meng retreated in haste toward his boats, but the hidden boats in the harbor soon seized his vessels and oars and raised Zhou banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 猛於是大敗，僅以身免，虜八千人。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon suffered great defeat, barely escaping with his life, capturing eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was utterly defeated, barely escaping with his life; eight thousand men were captured.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，司馬消難作亂，陰遣上開府段珣率兵陽為助守，因欲奪其城。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Sima Xiaonan rebelled; secretly he sent Upper Opener of the Government Duan Xun leading troops under pretense of aiding defense, intending thereby to seize the city.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu still served as Chancellor, Sima Xiaonan rebelled and secretly sent Upper Opener of the Government Duan Xun with troops who pretended to help defend the city but actually meant to seize it.

sentences.zh: 法尚覺其詐，閉門不納，珣遂圍之。

translations.literal: Fashang detected the deceit, closed the gates and refused entry, and Xun thereupon besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang saw through the ruse, shut the gates and refused to admit them, and Xun thereupon laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 于時倉卒，兵散在外，因率吏士五百人守拒二十日。

translations.literal: At that time it was sudden and hurried; troops were scattered outside, so he led five hundred clerks and soldiers to hold out in defense for twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard with his troops scattered elsewhere, he led five hundred clerks and soldiers and held the city for twenty days.

sentences.zh: 外無救援，自度力不能支，遂拔所領，棄城遁走。

translations.literal: With no relief from outside, judging his strength could not support him, he withdrew those he led, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With no relief coming from outside, he judged that he could not hold out, withdrew the men under his command, abandoned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 消難虜其母弟及家累三百人歸於陳。

translations.literal: Xiaonan captured his mother, younger brother, and household dependents—three hundred people—and took them to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan captured his mother, younger brother, and three hundred members of their household and took them back to Chen.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜巴州刺史，破三鵶叛蠻於鐵山，復從柱國王誼擊走陳寇。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, [Fashang] was appointed Administrator of Bazhou; he defeated the rebel Miao of Sanya at Tieshan, and again followed Pillar of State Wang Yi to drive off Chen raiders.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu accepted the throne, Fashang was appointed Administrator of Bazhou; he defeated the rebel tribes of Sanya at Iron Mountain and again followed Pillar of State Wang Yi in driving off Chen raiders.

sentences.zh: 遷衡州總管四州諸軍事，改封譙郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor-General of Hengzhou and military affairs of four prefectures; his title was changed to Duke of Qiao commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor-General of Hengzhou with authority over military affairs in four prefectures, and his title was changed to Duke of Qiao commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後上幸洛陽，召之，及引見，賜金鈿酒鐘一雙，彩五百段，良馬十五匹，奴婢三百口，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Later when the Emperor visited Luoyang, he summoned him; when granted audience, he bestowed a pair of gold-inlaid wine goblets, five hundred bolts of colored silk, fifteen fine horses, three hundred male and female servants, and granted one set of mounted musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Emperor visited Luoyang, he summoned Fashang; at their audience he gave him a pair of gold-inlaid wine goblets, five hundred bolts of colored silk, fifteen fine horses, three hundred servants, and a mounted musical escort.

sentences.zh: 法尚固辭，上曰：「公有大功于國，特給鼓吹者，欲令公鄉人知朕之寵公也。

translations.literal: Fashang firmly declined; the Emperor said: "You have great merit for the state. The mounted musical escort is granted especially so that the people of your native place may know that I favor you."
translations.idiomatic: Fashang firmly declined, but the Emperor said, "You have rendered great service to the state. I am granting you a mounted musical escort especially so that the people of your home district will know how highly I favor you."

sentences.zh: 」固與之。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly granted it to him anyway.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor insisted on granting it to him all the same.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉黃州總管。

translations.literal: After a little over a year, he was transferred to Governor-General of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later, he was transferred to Governor-General of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上降密詔，使經略江南，伺候動靜。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a secret edict ordering him to manage affairs in Jiangnan and watch for developments.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent down a secret edict ordering him to oversee Jiangnan and keep watch on conditions there.

sentences.zh: 及伐陳之役，以行軍總管隸秦孝王，率舟師三萬出於樊口。

translations.literal: During the campaign against Chen, as Mobile Campaign Commander under Prince Qin Xiao, he led thirty thousand naval troops out from Fankou.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Chen, serving as Mobile Campaign Commander under Prince Qin Xiao, he led thirty thousand naval troops out from Fankou.

sentences.zh: 陳城州刺史熊門超出師拒戰，擊破之，擒超於陣。

translations.literal: Chen's Administrator of Chengzhou Xiong Menchao marched out to resist battle; [Fashang] defeated him and captured Chao in the battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Menchao, Administrator of Chengzhou under Chen, marched out to give battle; Fashang defeated him and captured Chao on the field.

sentences.zh: 轉鄂州刺史，尋遷永州總管，安集嶺南，賜縑五百段，良馬五匹，仍給黃州兵三千五百人為帳內。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Ezhou; soon moved to Governor-General of Yongzhou to pacify and settle Lingnan; granted five hundred bolts of silk, five fine horses, and also given three thousand five hundred Huangzhou troops as his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Ezhou, then soon made Governor-General of Yongzhou to pacify Lingnan; he was granted five hundred bolts of silk and five fine horses, and also given three thousand five hundred Huangzhou troops as his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 陳桂州刺史錢季卿、南康內史柳璿、西衡州刺史鄧暠、陽山太守毛爽等前後詣法尚降。

translations.literal: Chen's Administrator of Guizhou Qian Jiqing, Administrator of Nankang Liu Xuan, Administrator of Xihengzhou Deng Gao, Administrator of Yangshan Mao Shuang, and others successively came to Fashang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jiqing, Administrator of Guizhou under Chen, Liu Xuan, Administrator of Nankang, Deng Gao, Administrator of Xihengzhou, Mao Shuang, Administrator of Yangshan, and others came one after another to surrender to Fashang.

sentences.zh: 陳定州刺史呂子廓據山洞反，法尚引兵逾嶺，子廓兵眾日散，與千餘人走保岩險，其左右斬之而降。

translations.literal: Chen's Administrator of Dingzhou Lü Zikuo seized mountain caves and rebelled; Fashang led troops over the ranges; Zikuo's forces daily dispersed; with a little over a thousand men he fled to hold rocky defiles; his attendants beheaded him and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zikuo, Administrator of Dingzhou under Chen, seized mountain strongholds and rebelled; Fashang led troops over the ranges, and Zikuo's forces dwindled day by day until he fled with a little over a thousand men to hold a rocky fastness, where his attendants beheaded him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賜彩五百段，奴婢五十口，並銀甕寶帶，良馬十匹。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of colored silk, fifty male and female servants, also a silver jar and precious belt, and ten fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted five hundred bolts of colored silk, fifty servants, a silver jar and precious belt, and ten fine horses.

sentences.zh: 十年，尋轉桂州總管，仍為嶺南安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, soon transferred to Governor-General of Guizhou, and also made Pacification Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was soon transferred to Governor-General of Guizhou and also made Pacification Commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 後數年入朝，以本官宿衛。

translations.literal: Several years later he came to court; with his original office he served as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he came to court and, retaining his original office, served in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 賜彩三百段，米五百石，絹五百匹。

translations.literal: Granted three hundred bolts of colored silk, five hundred shi of rice, and five hundred bolts of plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three hundred bolts of colored silk, five hundred shi of rice, and five hundred bolts of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 未幾，桂州人李光仕舉兵作亂，令法尚與上柱國王世積討之。

translations.literal: Before long, the Guizhou man Li Guangshi raised troops in rebellion; [the Emperor] ordered Fashang and Upper Pillar of State Wang Shiji to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Li Guangshi of Guizhou raised troops in rebellion, and the Emperor ordered Fashang and Upper Pillar of State Wang Shiji to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 法尚馳往桂州，發嶺南兵，世積出岳州，征嶺北軍，俱會于尹州。

translations.literal: Fashang hurried to Guizhou and mobilized Lingnan troops; Shiji went out from Yuezhou and summoned Lingbei armies; all met at Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang hurried to Guizhou and mobilized the troops of Lingnan, while Shiji marched out from Yuezhou and summoned the armies of Lingbei; the two forces met at Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 光仕來逆戰，擊走之。

translations.literal: Guangshi came to oppose battle; [they] struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi came out to give battle, but they struck him and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 世積所部多遇瘴，不能進，頓於衡州，法尚獨討之。

translations.literal: Shiji's subordinates mostly encountered miasma and could not advance; halted at Hengzhou; Fashang alone suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Shiji's troops fell victim to miasma and could not advance, so they halted at Hengzhou while Fashang alone pursued the suppression.

sentences.zh: 光仕帥勁兵保白石洞，法尚捕得其弟光略、光度，大獲家口。

translations.literal: Guangshi led elite troops to hold Baishi Cave; Fashang captured his younger brothers Guanglue and Guangdu, and seized many family members.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi led crack troops to hold Baishi Cave; Fashang captured his younger brothers Guanglue and Guangdu and seized a great many of their dependents.

sentences.zh: 其黨有來降附，輒以妻子還之。

translations.literal: When his partisans came to surrender, [Fashang] immediately returned their wives and children to them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever any of Guangshi's followers came over in surrender, Fashang immediately returned their wives and children to them.

sentences.zh: 居旬日，降者數千人。

translations.literal: Within ten days, several thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days, several thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 法尚捕兵列陣，以當光仕，親率奇兵，蔽林設伏。

translations.literal: Fashang deployed troops in battle array to face Guangshi, personally leading surprise troops to conceal themselves in the forest and set an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang drew up his main force to face Guangshi while personally leading an elite detachment to hide in the forest and lay an ambush.

sentences.zh: 兩陣始交，法尚馳擊其柵，柵中人皆走散，光仕大潰，追斬之。

translations.literal: When the two formations first clashed, Fashang charged to strike their palisade; everyone in the palisade scattered and fled; Guangshi was utterly routed and was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the two armies clashed, Fashang charged the palisade; the men inside scattered in flight, Guangshi was utterly routed, and he was pursued and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百五十口，黃金百五十兩，銀百五十斤。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred fifty male and female servants, one hundred fifty liang of gold, and one hundred fifty jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred fifty servants, one hundred fifty liang of gold, and one hundred fifty jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，遂州獠叛，復以行軍總管討平之。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era, the Liao of Suizhou rebelled; again as Mobile Campaign Commander he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou period, the Liao tribes of Suizhou rebelled, and again serving as Mobile Campaign Commander he suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 巂州烏蠻叛，攻陷州城，詔令法尚便道擊之。

translations.literal: The Wuman of Xizhou rebelled and captured the prefectural city; an edict ordered Fashang to strike them by the nearest route.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Barbarians of Xizhou rebelled and captured the prefectural city, and an edict ordered Fashang to attack them by the nearest route.

sentences.zh: 軍將至，賊棄州城，散走山谷間，法尚捕不能得。

translations.literal: When the army was about to arrive, the bandits abandoned the prefectural city and scattered fleeing among mountain valleys; Fashang could not capture them.
translations.idiomatic: As his army was nearing the city, the rebels abandoned it and scattered into the mountain valleys, and Fashang could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使慰諭，假以官號，偽班師，日行二十里。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to comfort and instruct them, granted them nominal official titles, feigned withdrawal of the army, and marched twenty li per day.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent envoys to reassure them, granted them nominal official titles, feigned a withdrawal, and marched only twenty li a day.

sentences.zh: 軍再舍，潛遣人覘之，知其首領盡歸柵，聚飲相賀。

translations.literal: After the army camped twice, he secretly sent men to spy and learned that their chieftains had all returned to the palisade and gathered to drink in mutual celebration.
translations.idiomatic: After the army had made two camps, he secretly sent scouts and learned that the rebel chieftains had all returned to their stockade and were gathered there drinking in celebration.

sentences.zh: 法尚選步騎數千人，襲擊破之，獲其渠帥數千人，虜男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: Fashang selected several thousand infantry and cavalry, made a surprise attack and defeated them, captured several thousand of their chieftains, and took captive more than ten thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang selected several thousand infantry and cavalry, launched a surprise attack and routed them, captured several thousand chieftains, and took more than ten thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百口，物三百段，蜀馬二十匹。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred male and female servants, three hundred bundles of goods, and twenty Shu horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred servants, three hundred bundles of goods, and twenty Shu horses.

sentences.zh: 軍還，檢校潞州事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he inspected and managed affairs of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was put in charge of affairs at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉雲州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, [Fashang] was transferred to Administrator of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Fashang was transferred to Administrator of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，轉定襄太守，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Three years later, transferred to Administrator of Dingxiang; advanced in rank to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was made Administrator of Dingxiang and advanced to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 時帝幸榆林，法尚朝於行宮。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was visiting Yulin; Fashang attended court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor was at Yulin, and Fashang came to audience at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 內史令元壽言於帝曰：「漢武出塞，旍旗千里。

translations.literal: Inner Secretariat Director Yuan Shou said to the Emperor: "When Emperor Wu of Han went beyond the frontier, his banners and flags stretched for a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretariat Director Yuan Shou said to the Emperor, "When Emperor Wu of Han marched beyond the frontier, his banners and flags stretched for a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 今御營之外，請分為二十四軍，日別遣一軍發，相去三十里，旗幟相望，鉦鼓相聞，首尾連注，千里不絕。

translations.literal: "Beyond the imperial encampment, let it be divided into twenty-four armies; each day one army is dispatched separately, thirty li apart, banners and flags visible to one another, gongs and drums heard by one another, head and tail linked in succession, unbroken for a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond the imperial encampment, I propose dividing the force into twenty-four armies, dispatching one army each day thirty li apart so that banners and flags are visible to one another and gongs and drums can be heard from end to end, linking head and tail in an unbroken line for a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 此亦出師之盛者也。

translations.literal: "This too would be the splendor of an army on campaign."
translations.idiomatic: "That too would be a magnificent display for an army on campaign."

sentences.zh: 」法尚曰：「不然，兵亙千里，動間山川，卒有不虞，四分五裂。

translations.literal: Fashang said: "Not so. An army stretched across a thousand li, with mountains and rivers intervening in its movements—if suddenly something unforeseen occurs, it will split four ways and five ways."
translations.idiomatic: Fashang said, "That is not so. An army strung out for a thousand li, with mountains and rivers breaking up its movements, will splinter at the first unexpected blow."

sentences.zh: 腹心有事，首尾未知，道阻且長，難以相救。

translations.literal: "If the center has trouble, head and tail will not know; the route is blocked and long—it will be hard to rescue one another."
translations.idiomatic: "If trouble strikes the center, the front and rear will not even know; the roads are obstructed and long, and mutual rescue will be impossible."

sentences.zh: 雖是故事，此乃取敗之道也。

translations.literal: "Although this is an old precedent, it is a path to defeat."
translations.idiomatic: "Even though this follows an old precedent, it is a recipe for defeat."

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌曰：「卿意以為如何？

translations.literal: The Emperor, displeased, said: "What do you think should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, displeased, said, "What do you think ought to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」法尚曰：「結為方陣，四面外距，六宮及百官家口並住其間。

translations.literal: Fashang said: "Form a square formation, resist outward on four sides; the six palaces and the household dependents of all officials all dwell within it."
translations.idiomatic: Fashang said, "Form a square camp and face outward on all four sides, with the six palaces and the households of all officials placed within it."

sentences.zh: 若有變起，當頭分抗，內引奇兵，出外奮擊，車為壁壘，重設鉤陳，此與據城理亦何異！

translations.literal: "If trouble arises, meet it head-on at the front in divided resistance; draw elite troops from within and strike fiercely outside; wagons serve as ramparts and the Gouchen formation is set in depth—how is this in principle different from holding a city!"
translations.idiomatic: "If trouble arises, meet it with divided resistance at the front while drawing elite troops from within to strike fiercely outside; wagons serve as ramparts and the Gouchen formation is deployed in depth—how is that in principle any different from holding a city!"

sentences.zh: 若戰而捷，抽騎追奔，或戰不利，屯營自守。

translations.literal: "If battle is victorious, detach cavalry to pursue the fleeing; if battle goes badly, encamp and hold on one's own."
translations.idiomatic: "If the battle goes well, detach cavalry to pursue the fleeing enemy; if it goes badly, hold the camp and stand on the defensive."

sentences.zh: 臣謂牢固萬全之策也。

translations.literal: "I consider this a firm and fully secure strategy."
translations.idiomatic: "In my view, that is a firm and fully secure strategy."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」因拜左武衛將軍，賜良馬一匹，絹三百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Fashang] was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard; granted one fine horse and three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fashang was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and granted one fine horse and three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 明年，黔安夷向思多反，殺將軍鹿願，圍太守蕭造，法尚與將軍李景分路討之。

translations.literal: The next year, the Qian'an Yi Xiang Siduo rebelled, killed General Lu Yuan, and besieged Administrator Xiao Zao; Fashang and General Li Jing suppressed him by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Qian'an tribesman Xiang Siduo rebelled, killed General Lu Yuan, and besieged Administrator Xiao Zao; Fashang and General Li Jing suppressed him by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 法尚擊思多於清江，破之，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: Fashang struck Siduo at the Qing River, defeated him, and beheaded three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang attacked Siduo on the Qing River, defeated him, and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 還，從討吐谷渾，法尚別出松州道，逐捕亡散，至於青海。

translations.literal: Returning, he followed the campaign against Tuyuhun; Fashang separately went out by the Songzhou route, pursuing and capturing scattered fugitives as far as Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he joined the campaign against Tuyuhun; Fashang marched separately by the Songzhou route, pursuing scattered fugitives as far as Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢一百口，物二百段，馬七十匹。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred male and female servants, two hundred bundles of goods, and seventy horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred servants, two hundred bundles of goods, and seventy horses.

sentences.zh: 出為敦煌太守，尋領會甯太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Dunhuang; soon also held concurrently Administrator of Huining.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as Administrator of Dunhuang and soon also held the concurrent post of Administrator of Huining.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以舟師指朝鮮道，會楊玄感反，與將軍宇文述，來護兒等破之。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, with the naval force pointing toward the Korea route, encountering Yang Xuangan's rebellion, together with Generals Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and others he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, while commanding the naval force toward Korea, he turned back when Yang Xuangan rebelled and, together with Generals Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and others, defeated him.

sentences.zh: 以功進右光祿大夫，賜物九百段。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendor of the Right; granted nine hundred bundles of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendor of the Right and granted nine hundred bundles of goods.

sentences.zh: 時有齊郡人王薄、孟讓等舉兵為盜，眾十餘萬，保長白山。

translations.literal: At that time there were men of Qi commandery Wang Bo, Meng Rang, and others who raised troops as bandits, a host of more than a hundred thousand, holding Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Bo, Meng Rang, and others of Qi commandery raised troops as bandits; their force numbered more than a hundred thousand, and they held Changbai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 頻戰，每挫其銳。

translations.literal: [He] fought repeatedly and each time blunted their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: He fought them repeatedly and each time blunted their momentum.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百口。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred servants.

sentences.zh: 明年，復臨滄海，在軍疾甚，謂長史崔君肅曰：「吾再臨滄海，未能利涉，時不我與，將辭人世。

translations.literal: The next year, again facing the eastern sea, gravely ill in the army, he said to Chief Clerk Cui Junsu: "I have twice come to the eastern sea yet have been unable to cross profitably; time does not wait for me—I am about to leave the world of men."
translations.idiomatic: The next year, once again on the coast, he fell gravely ill in camp and said to Chief Clerk Cui Junsu, "I have twice come to the eastern sea yet never managed a successful crossing; time will not wait for me—I am about to leave this world."

sentences.zh: 立志不果，命也如何！

translations.literal: "My resolve unfulfilled—such is fate, what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: "My ambition remains unfulfilled—such is fate; what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 」言畢而終，時年五十九。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he died; he was fifty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He finished speaking and died; he was fifty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 贈武衛大將軍，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Great General of the Martial Guard; posthumous name Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Great General of the Martial Guard and given the posthumous name Xi.

sentences.zh: 有子六人。

translations.literal: He had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子紹基，靈壽令，少子紹范，最知名。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shaoji was Magistrate of Lingshou; the youngest son Shaofan was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shaoji was Magistrate of Lingshou; his youngest son Shaofan was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 李景，字道興，天水休官人也。

translations.literal: Li Jing, styled Daoxing, was a native of Xiuguan in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, styled Daoxing, was a native of Xiuguan in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父超，周應、戎二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chao was Administrator of the two prefectures Ying and Rong under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao had served as Administrator of Ying and Rong under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 景容貌奇偉，膂力過人，美須髯，驍勇善射。

translations.literal: Jing's appearance was remarkably imposing; his physical strength surpassed others; he had a fine beard and whiskers; he was fierce and brave and skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had a strikingly imposing appearance, strength beyond ordinary men, a handsome beard and whiskers, and was fierce, brave, and skilled with the bow.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，頗有力焉，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi he contributed considerably; he was appointed Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Qi he distinguished himself and was appointed Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 以平尉迥，進位開府，賜爵平寇縣公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: For pacifying Yuwen Yong he advanced to Opener of the Government; granted the title Duke of Pingkou county with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Yuwen Yong he was promoted to Opener of the Government and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingkou county with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，以行軍總管從王世積伐陳，陷陳有功，進位上開府，賜奴婢六十口，物千五百段。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, as Mobile Campaign Commander he followed Wang Shiji to attack Chen; penetrating Chen he had merit; advanced to Upper Opener of the Government; granted sixty male and female servants and one thousand five hundred bundles of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, serving as Mobile Campaign Commander under Wang Shiji in the attack on Chen, he distinguished himself in the assault on Chen, was promoted to Upper Opener of the Government, and was granted sixty servants and one thousand five hundred bundles of goods.

sentences.zh: 及高智慧等作亂江南，復以行軍總管從楊素擊之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, again as Mobile Campaign Commander he followed Yang Su to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, he again served as Mobile Campaign Commander under Yang Su in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 別平倉嶺，還授鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: Separately he pacified Cangcang Ridge; on return appointed Administrator of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He separately pacified Cangcang Ridge and, on his return, was appointed Administrator of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遼東之役，為馬軍總管。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, during the Liaodong campaign, he was Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, during the Liaodong campaign, he served as Cavalry Commander.

sentences.zh: 及還，配事漢王。

translations.literal: When he returned, he was assigned to serve the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he was assigned to serve the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 高祖奇其壯武，使袒而觀之，曰：「卿相表當位極人臣。

translations.literal: Gaozu marveled at his stalwart martial bearing, had him bare his torso to look at him, and said: "Your physiognomy shows you should reach the supreme rank among ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu marveled at his stalwart build, had him bare his torso for inspection, and said, "Your physiognomy shows that you are destined to reach the highest rank among ministers."

sentences.zh: 」尋從史萬歲擊突厥於大斤山，別路邀賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Shi Wansui to strike the Turks at Mt. Dajin; by a separate route he intercepted the bandits and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Shi Wansui in attacking the Turks at Mount Dajin; marching by a separate route he intercepted the enemy and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 後與上明公楊紀送義成公主于突厥，至恆安，遇突厥來寇。

translations.literal: Later together with Duke of Shangming Yang Ji he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Turks; reaching Heng'an, they encountered Turks coming to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Duke of Shangming Yang Ji, he escorted Princess Yicheng to the Turks; at Heng'an they encountered a Turkish raiding force.

sentences.zh: 時代州總管韓洪為虜所敗，景率所領數百人援之。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General of Daizhou Han Hong was defeated by the enemy; Jing led several hundred men under his command to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor-General of Daizhou Han Hong had been defeated by the enemy, and Jing led several hundred men under his command to his relief.

sentences.zh: 力戰三日，殺虜甚眾，賜物三千段，授韓州刺史。

translations.literal: After fighting fiercely for three days, he killed a great many of the enemy; granted three thousand bundles of goods; appointed Administrator of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three days of fierce fighting he killed a great many of the enemy; he was granted three thousand bundles of goods and appointed Administrator of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以事王故，不之官。

translations.literal: Because he was serving the Prince, he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was still serving the Prince, he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，檢校代州總管。

translations.literal: During Renshou, he inspected and managed as Governor-General of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou period he served as acting Governor-General of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒作亂并州，景發兵拒之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han Liang rebelled at Bingzhou, Jing mobilized troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled at Bingzhou, Jing mobilized troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 諒遣劉暠襲景，戰於城東。

translations.literal: Liang sent Liu Kui to attack Jing; they fought east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Liu Kui to attack Jing, and they fought east of the city.

sentences.zh: 升樓射之，無不應弦而倒。

translations.literal: [Jing] mounted the tower and shot at them; none failed to fall at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Jing mounted the tower and shot at them; every arrow found its mark and the men fell as the bowstrings sounded.

sentences.zh: 選壯士擊之，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: He selected stalwart warriors to strike them; killed and captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected stalwart warriors to sally forth against them and killed or captured nearly all of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諒復遣嵐州刺史喬鐘葵率勁勇三萬攻之。

translations.literal: Liang again sent Administrator of Lanzhou Qiao Zhongkui leading thirty thousand crack troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang again sent Qiao Zhongkui, Administrator of Lanzhou, with thirty thousand crack troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 景戰士不過數千，加以城池不固，為賊衝擊，崩毀相繼。

translations.literal: Jing's warriors numbered no more than several thousand; moreover the city walls were not solid; struck by the bandits, sections collapsed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had no more than a few thousand fighters, and the city walls were weak besides; under the enemy assault, sections of wall collapsed one after another.

sentences.zh: 景且戰且築，士卒皆殊死鬥，屢挫賊鋒。

translations.literal: Jing fought while building; soldiers all fought to the death; repeatedly blunted the bandits' sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fought even as he rebuilt the walls; his soldiers fought to the death and repeatedly blunted the enemy assault.

sentences.zh: 司馬馮孝慈、司法參軍呂玉並驍勇善戰，儀同三司侯莫陳乂多謀畫，工拒守之術。

translations.literal: Major Feng Xiaoci and Judicial Assistant Lü Yu were both fierce and brave and skilled in battle; Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank Hou Mochen Yi was full of stratagems and skilled in the art of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Major Feng Xiaoci and Judicial Assistant Lü Yu were both fierce and skilled in battle; Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank Hou Mochen Yi was resourceful and expert in defensive warfare.

sentences.zh: 景知將士可用，其後推誠於此三人，無所關預，唯在閣持重，時出撫循而已。

translations.literal: Jing knew the officers and soldiers could be employed; thereafter he gave his trust entirely to these three men without interfering at all; he only sat in the pavilion with gravity, occasionally going out to comfort and reassure them, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Jing knew his officers and men could be relied upon; thereafter he entrusted everything to these three men without interfering, sitting gravely in the pavilion and only going out from time to time to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 月餘，朔州總管楊義臣以兵來援，合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Governor-General of Shuozhou Yang Yichen came with troops to relieve them; joining in attack, they utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, Governor-General of Shuozhou Yang Yichen arrived with relief troops; joining forces, they inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 先是，景府內井中甃上生花如蓮，並有龍見，時變為鐵馬甲士。

translations.literal: Before this, on the brickwork of a well within Jing's headquarters flowers like lotuses had grown, and a dragon was seen; at times it transformed into armored soldiers on iron horses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, lotus-like flowers had appeared on the brickwork of a well inside Jing's headquarters, and a dragon was seen there; at times it changed into armored soldiers mounted on iron horses.

sentences.zh: 又有神人長數丈見於城下，其跡長四尺五寸。

translations.literal: Also a divine being several zhang tall was seen below the city; its footprints were four chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: A divine being several zhang tall was also seen below the city, leaving footprints four chi five cun long.

sentences.zh: 景問巫，對曰：「此是不祥之物，來食人血耳。

translations.literal: Jing questioned the shamans, who replied: "This is an inauspicious thing that has come to feed on human blood."
translations.idiomatic: Jing questioned the shamans, who answered, "This is an inauspicious creature come to feed on human blood."

sentences.zh: 」景大怒，推出之。

translations.literal: Jing flew into a great rage and had them driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing flew into a rage and had them driven out.

sentences.zh: 旬日而兵至，死者數萬焉。

translations.literal: Within ten days troops arrived, and those who died numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the army arrived, and tens of thousands died.

sentences.zh: 景尋被征入京，進位柱國，拜右武衛大將軍，賜縑九千匹，女樂一部，加以珍物。

translations.literal: Before long Jing was summoned to the capital, advanced to Pillar of State, appointed Right General of the Wuwei Guards, granted nine thousand bolts of silk, one ensemble of female musicians, and precious items besides.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jing was summoned to the capital, promoted to Pillar of State, and appointed Right General of the Wuwei Guards; he received nine thousand bolts of silk, a troupe of female musicians, and other precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 景智略非所長，而忠直為時所許，帝甚信之。

translations.literal: Jing was not particularly strong in strategy and tactics, but his loyalty and uprightness were praised by the age, and the emperor greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was not especially gifted in strategy, but his loyalty and integrity won wide esteem, and the emperor placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 擊叛蠻向思多，破之，賜奴婢八十口。

translations.literal: He attacked the rebellious barbarian Xiang Siduo, defeated him, and was granted eighty male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the rebel chieftain Xiang Siduo, defeated him, and was rewarded with eighty male and female slaves.

sentences.zh: 明年，擊吐谷渾于青海，破之，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The following year he attacked the Tuyuhun at Qinghai Lake, defeated them, and was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked the Tuyuhun at Qinghai Lake, routed them, and was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢六十口，縑二千匹。

translations.literal: He was granted sixty male and female slaves and two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He received sixty male and female slaves and two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西巡，至天水，景獻食於帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the imperial carriage made a western tour to Tianshui, Jing presented food to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, during the emperor's western tour to Tianshui, Jing presented a feast to him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公，主人也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You, sir, are the host."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You, sir, are the host here."

sentences.zh: 」賜坐齊王暕之上。

translations.literal: He granted him a seat above Prince of Qi Yang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a seat above Prince of Qi Yang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 至隴川宮，帝將大獵，景與左武衛大將軍郭衍俱有難言，為人所奏。

translations.literal: At Longchuan Palace, when the emperor was about to hold a great hunt, Jing and Left General of the Wuwei Guards Guo Yan both had words hard to speak, and someone reported them.
translations.idiomatic: At Longchuan Palace, when the emperor was preparing a great hunt, Jing and Left General of the Wuwei Guards Guo Yan both voiced private objections, and someone reported them.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，令左右Ξ之，竟以坐免。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to beat them; in the end he was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to beat them; Jing was ultimately dismissed from office on that charge.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復位，與宇文述等參掌選舉。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to office and, with Yuwen Shu and others, jointly managed appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was restored to office and, together with Yuwen Shu and others, shared responsibility for official appointments.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻高麗武厲城，破之，賜爵苑丘侯，物一千段。

translations.literal: The following year he attacked Wuli city in Goguryeo, captured it, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanqiu with one thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Wuli in Goguryeo, took the city, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuanqiu with a grant of one thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 八年，出渾彌道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he marched out by the Hunmi route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched out by the Hunmi route.

sentences.zh: 九年，復出遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again marched out to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again marched into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 及旋師，以景為殿。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Jing was made rearguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, Jing was assigned to command the rearguard.

sentences.zh: 高麗追兵大至，景擊走之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo pursuit troops arrived in force; Jing struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo pursuit troops came up in force, but Jing attacked and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賚物三千段，進爵滑國公。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of goods and advanced in rank to Duke of Huaguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of goods and promoted to Duke of Huaguo.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反也，朝臣子弟多預焉，而景獨無關涉。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, many sons of court officials were implicated, but Jing alone had no connection.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, many sons of court officials were implicated, but Jing alone had no part in it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公誠直天然，我之梁棟也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You, sir, are upright by nature—my pillar and beam."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You, sir, are upright by nature—you are my mainstay."

sentences.zh: 」賜以美女。

translations.literal: He was granted beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with beautiful women.

sentences.zh: 帝每呼李大將軍而不名，其見重如此。

translations.literal: The emperor always called him "General Li" without naming him; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always addressed him as "General Li" without using his given name—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝令景營遼東戰具于北平，賜御馬一匹，名師子𩢴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor ordered Jing to prepare Liaodong war equipment at Beiping and granted him an imperial horse named Shizi Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor ordered Jing to prepare Liaodong war materiel at Beiping and granted him an imperial horse named Shizi Tuo.

sentences.zh: 會幽州賊楊仲緒率眾萬餘人來攻北平，景督兵擊破之，斬仲緒。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel of Youzhou, Yang Zhongxu, led more than ten thousand men to attack Beiping; Jing led troops and defeated them, beheading Zhongxu.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Youzhou rebel Yang Zhongxu led more than ten thousand men to attack Beiping; Jing commanded the troops, defeated them, and beheaded Zhongxu.

sentences.zh: 于時盜賊蜂起，道路隔絕，景遂召募，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere and roads were cut off; Jing thereupon recruited men to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere and roads were cut off; Jing thereupon recruited troops to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將羅藝與景有隙，遂誣景將反。

translations.literal: Military Guards Brigade Vice Commander Luo Yi had a grudge against Jing and falsely accused him of intending rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Vice Commander of the Military Guards Luo Yi bore a grudge against Jing and falsely accused him of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝遣其子慰諭之曰：「縱人言公窺天闕，據京師，吾無疑也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent his son to reassure him, saying, "Even if people say you covet the imperial palace and would seize the capital, I have no doubt of you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his son to reassure him, saying, "Even if people say you are eyeing the imperial palace and mean to seize the capital, I do not doubt you."

sentences.zh: 」後為高開道所圍，獨守孤城，外無聲援，歲餘，士卒患腳腫而死者十將六七，景撫循之，一無離叛。

translations.literal: Later he was besieged by Gao Kaodao, holding a lone city with no support from outside; after more than a year, six or seven out of ten soldiers died of swollen feet, yet Jing comforted and cared for them and not one deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was besieged by Gao Kaodao and held a lone city with no relief from outside; after more than a year, six or seven out of ten soldiers died of swollen feet, yet Jing comforted and cared for them and not one deserted.

sentences.zh: 遼東軍資多在其所，粟帛山積，既逢離亂，景無所私焉。

translations.literal: Much of the Liaodong army's supplies were stored at his post; grain and cloth piled mountain-high, yet amid the disorder Jing took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the Liaodong campaign's supplies were stored at his post, with grain and cloth piled like mountains, yet amid the chaos Jing took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩于江都，遼西太守鄧暠率兵救之，遂歸柳城。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Governor of Liaoxi Deng Hao led troops to rescue him, and he then returned to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Governor of Liaoxi Deng Hao led troops to relieve him, and Jing then returned to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 後將還幽州，在道遇賊，見害。

translations.literal: Later, as he was about to return to Youzhou, he met bandits on the road and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as he was returning to Youzhou, he was killed by bandits on the road.

sentences.zh: 契丹、靺軻素感其恩，聞之莫不流涕，幽、燕人士於今傷惜之。

translations.literal: The Khitan and Mohe, who had long felt his kindness, all wept when they heard of it; people of You and Yan mourn him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan and Mohe, who had long felt his kindness, wept when they heard the news; people of You and Yan still mourn him to this day.

sentences.zh: 有子世謨。

translations.literal: He had a son named Shimò.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Shimò.

sentences.zh: 慕容三藏

translations.literal: Murong Sancang
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sancang

sentences.zh: 慕容三藏，燕人也。

translations.literal: Murong Sancang was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sancang was a native of Yan.

sentences.zh: 父紹宗，齊尚書左僕射、東南道大行台。

translations.literal: His father Shaozong was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaozong had been Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner of the Southeast Circuit under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 三藏幼聰敏，多武略，頗有父風。

translations.literal: Sancang was clever and quick-witted from youth, gifted in military affairs, and very much in his father's mold.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Sancang was clever and quick-witted, skilled in military affairs, and very much in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，釋褐太尉府參軍事，尋遷備身都督。

translations.literal: He entered Qi service, beginning his career as an aide in the Grand Marshal's office and soon advancing to bodyguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under Qi, beginning his career as an aide in the Grand Marshal's office and soon rising to bodyguard commander.

sentences.zh: 武平初，襲爵燕郡公，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he inherited the title Duke of Yancheng with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuping era he inherited the title Duke of Yancheng with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年，敗周師于孝水，又破陳師于壽陽，轉武衛將軍。

translations.literal: That year he defeated Zhou troops at Xiaoshui and also defeated Chen troops at Shouyang, and was transferred to General of the Wuwei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: That year he defeated Zhou troops at Xiaoshui and Chen troops at Shouyang, and was transferred to General of the Wuwei Guards.

sentences.zh: 又敗周師于河陽，授武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He again defeated Zhou troops at Heyang and was appointed General of the Wuwei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Zhou troops at Heyang and was appointed General of the Wuwei Guards.

sentences.zh: 又轉右衛將軍，別封范陽縣公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to General of the Right Guards, separately enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to General of the Right Guards and separately enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 周師入鄴也，齊後主失守東遁，委三藏等留守鄴宮。
