translations.literal: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Northern Qi's last ruler lost the capital and fled east, entrusting Sancang and others to hold Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops entered Ye, the last ruler of Northern Qi lost the capital and fled east, leaving Sancang and others to hold the palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊之王公以下皆降，三藏猶率麾下抗拒周師。

translations.literal: Princes and officials of Qi down to the lowest ranks all surrendered, but Sancang still led his followers to resist the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and officials of Qi down to the lowest ranks all surrendered, but Sancang still led his followers in resisting the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，武帝引見，恩禮甚厚，詔曰：「三藏父子誠節著聞，宜加榮秩。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, Emperor Wu of Zhou received him in audience with great kindness and issued an edict: "The loyal integrity of Sancang and his father is well known; they should be granted honorable rank."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was pacified, Emperor Wu of Zhou received him in audience with great favor and issued an edict: "The loyal integrity of Sancang and his father is well known; they should be granted honorable rank."

sentences.zh: 」授開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General for Opening the Court with Equal Standing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General for Opening the Court with Equal Standing.

sentences.zh: 其年，稽胡叛，令三藏討平之。

translations.literal: That year the Ji Hu rebelled; he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ji Hu rebelled, and he was ordered to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，授吳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，奉詔持節涼州道黜陟大使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he received an imperial edict to serve as inspection commissioner for promotions and demotions on the Liangzhou circuit, bearing the credentials of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered by imperial edict to serve as inspection commissioner for promotions and demotions on the Liangzhou circuit, bearing the credentials of office.

sentences.zh: 其年，嶺南酋長王仲宣反，圍廣州，詔令柱國、襄陽公韋洸為行軍總管，三藏為副。

translations.literal: That year the chieftain of Lingnan, Wang Zhongxuan, rebelled and besieged Guangzhou; an edict appointed Pillar of State and Duke of Xiangyang Wei Kuang as campaigning commander-in-chief, with Sancang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Lingnan chieftain Wang Zhongxuan rebelled and besieged Guangzhou; an edict appointed Pillar of State and Duke of Xiangyang Wei Kuang as campaigning commander-in-chief, with Sancang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至廣州，與賊交戰，洸為流矢所中，卒，詔令三藏檢校廣州道行軍事。

translations.literal: When they reached Guangzhou and fought the rebels, Kuang was struck by a stray arrow and died; an edict made Sancang acting commander of military affairs on the Guangzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Guangzhou and fought the rebels, Kuang was struck by a stray arrow and died; an edict put Sancang in charge of military affairs on the Guangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年，賊眾四面攻圍，三藏固守月餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the rebel host attacked from all sides and besieged the city; Sancang held firm for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the rebels attacked from all sides and besieged the city; Sancang held firm for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 城中糧少矢盡，三藏以為不可持久，遂自率驍銳，夜出突圍擊之。

translations.literal: Provisions in the city ran low and arrows were exhausted; Sancang judged that the situation could not last, so he personally led crack troops and sallied out by night to break the encirclement and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions in the city ran low and arrows were exhausted; Sancang judged that the siege could not be endured, so he personally led crack troops in a night sortie to break the encirclement and attack.

sentences.zh: 賊眾敗散，廣州獲全。

translations.literal: The rebel host was routed and scattered, and Guangzhou was saved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and scattered, and Guangzhou was saved.

sentences.zh: 以功授大將軍，賜奴婢百口，加以金銀雜物。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General-in-Chief and granted one hundred male and female slaves together with gold, silver, and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed General-in-Chief and granted one hundred male and female slaves, along with gold, silver, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授廓州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed Governor of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 州極西界，與吐谷渾鄰接，奸宄犯法者皆遷配彼州，流人多有逃逸。

translations.literal: The prefecture lay at the far western border, adjoining Tuyuhun; criminals and wrongdoers were all exiled there, and many exiles fled.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay at the far western frontier, bordering Tuyuhun; criminals were exiled there, and many exiles escaped.

sentences.zh: 及三藏至，招納綏撫，百姓愛悅，繦負日至，吏民歌頌之。

translations.literal: When Sancang arrived he recruited and pacified them; the people came to love and delight in him, children carried on backs arrived daily, and officials and commoners sang his praises.
translations.idiomatic: When Sancang arrived he recruited and pacified the people; they came to love and trust him, families arrived daily with children on their backs, and officials and commoners sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞其能，屢有勞問。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard of his ability and repeatedly sent messages expressing appreciation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu heard of his ability and repeatedly sent messages of appreciation.

sentences.zh: 其年，當州畜產繁孳，獲醍醐奉獻，賚物百段。

translations.literal: That year livestock in the prefecture bred abundantly; ghee was obtained and presented in tribute, and he was rewarded with one hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: That year livestock in the prefecture bred abundantly; ghee was obtained and presented in tribute, and he was rewarded with one hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 十三年，州界連雲山響，稱萬年者三，詔頒郡國，仍遣使醮於山所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Lianyun Mountain in the prefecture resounded, thrice proclaiming "ten thousand years"; an edict was promulgated to the commanderies and kingdoms, and envoys were still dispatched to perform sacrificial rites at the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Lianyun Mountain in the prefecture resounded, thrice proclaiming "ten thousand years"; an edict was sent to the commanderies and kingdoms, and envoys were dispatched to perform sacrificial rites at the mountain.

sentences.zh: 其日景雲浮於上，雉間兔馴壇側，使還具以聞，上大悅。

translations.literal: That day auspicious clouds floated above; pheasants mingled and rabbits were tame beside the altar; when the envoy returned and reported fully, the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: That day auspicious clouds floated above; pheasants mingled and rabbits were tame beside the altar; when the envoy returned and reported in full, the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授疊州總管。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Governor-General of Diezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Governor-General of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 党項羌時有翻叛，三藏隨便討平之，部內夷夏咸得安輯。

translations.literal: The Tangut Qiang rebelled from time to time; Sancang suppressed them wherever needed, and within his jurisdiction both barbarians and Chinese were settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut Qiang rebelled from time to time; Sancang suppressed them as needed, and within his jurisdiction both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，改封河內縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou his fief was changed to Baron of Henei county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou his title was changed to Baron of Henei county.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，授和州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye he was appointed Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye he was appointed Governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉任淮南郡太守，所在有惠政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Administrator of Huainan commandery; wherever he served he showed kind governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Administrator of Huainan commandery; wherever he served he governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 其年，改授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year he was changed to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 大業七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Daye.

sentences.zh: 三藏從子遐，為澶水丞，漢王反，抗節不從，以誠節聞。

translations.literal: Sancang's nephew by younger brother lineage, Xia, was Deputy Magistrate of the Zhan River; when Prince of Han rebelled, he upheld his integrity and would not follow, and was known for loyal steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Sancang's nephew Xia was deputy magistrate of the Zhan River; when Prince of Han rebelled, he upheld his integrity and refused to follow, and was known for loyal steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 薛世雄

translations.literal: Xue Shixiong
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shixiong

sentences.zh: 薛世雄，字世英，本河東汾陰人也，其先寓居關中。

translations.literal: Xue Shixiong, styled Shiying, was originally from Fenyin in Hedong; his ancestors had long resided in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shixiong, styled Shiying, was originally from Fenyin in Hedong; his family had long lived in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 父回，字道弘，仕周，官至涇州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hui, styled Daohong, served Zhou and rose to Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui, styled Daohong, served Zhou and rose to Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，封舞陰郡公，領漕渠監，以年老致事，終於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed Duke of Wuyin commandery, held the post of Superintendent of the Transport Canal, retired on account of old age, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed Duke of Wuyin commandery, served as superintendent of the transport canal, retired on account of old age, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 世雄為兒童時，與群輩遊戲，輒畫地為城郭，令諸兒為攻守之勢，有不從令者，世雄輒撻之，諸兒畏憚，莫不齊整。

translations.literal: When Shixiong was a child, playing with his companions he would trace cities and walls on the ground and assign the other boys to attack and defend; any who disobeyed his orders Shixiong would whip, and the boys feared him—all fell into proper ranks.
translations.idiomatic: As a child, when Shixiong played with his companions he would trace cities and walls on the ground and set the other boys to attack and defend; any who disobeyed he would whip, and the boys feared him so much that all fell into proper ranks.

sentences.zh: 其父見而奇之，謂人曰：「此兒當興吾家矣。

translations.literal: His father saw this and marveled, saying to people, "This boy will revive our house."
translations.idiomatic: His father saw this and marveled, saying to others, "This boy will revive our house."

sentences.zh: 」年十七，從周武帝平齊，以功拜帥都督。

translations.literal: At seventeen he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in the pacification of Qi and, for merit, was appointed Commander of the Wielders of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in the pacification of Qi and, for his merit, was appointed commander of the wielders of authority.

sentences.zh: 開皇時，數有戰功，累遷儀同三司、右親衛車騎將軍。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he repeatedly won military honors and was promoted in succession to Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank and Right Guard Cavalry General of the Imperial Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he won repeated military honors and rose in succession to Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank and Right Guard Cavalry General of the Imperial Attendants.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，番禺夷、獠相聚為亂，詔世雄討平之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, the Yi and Liao of Panyu gathered in rebellion; an edict ordered Shixiong to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, the Yi and Liao of Panyu gathered in rebellion; an edict ordered Shixiong to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 遷右監門郎將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commander of the Door Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commander of the Door Guard.

sentences.zh: 從帝征吐谷渾，進位通議大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun and was promoted to Master for Direct Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Tuyuhun and was promoted to Master for Direct Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 世雄性廉謹，凡所行軍破敵之處，秋毫無犯，帝由是嘉之。

translations.literal: Shixiong was incorruptible and careful by nature; wherever his armies marched and defeated the enemy they took not the slightest thing, and the emperor therefore commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong was incorruptible and careful by nature; wherever his armies marched and defeated the enemy they took not the slightest thing, and the emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容謂群臣曰：「我欲舉好人，未知諸君識不？

translations.literal: The emperor once said casually to his ministers, "I wish to promote a worthy man—do you gentlemen know who I mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said casually to his ministers, "I wish to promote a worthy man—do you know who I have in mind?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸曰：「臣等何能測聖心。

translations.literal: The ministers all said, "How could we fathom the sage mind?"
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said, "How could we fathom the sage mind?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我欲舉者薛世雄。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The man I wish to promote is Xue Shixiong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The man I wish to promote is Xue Shixiong."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆稱善。

translations.literal: The ministers all praised the choice.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all praised the choice.

sentences.zh: 帝復曰：「世雄廉正節概，有古人之風。

translations.literal: The emperor again said, "Shixiong is incorrupt, upright, and high-minded—he has the air of men of old."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added, "Shixiong is incorrupt, upright, and high-minded—he has the bearing of men of old."

sentences.zh: 」於是超拜右翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was exceptionally promoted to General of the Right Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was exceptionally promoted to General of the Right Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以世雄為玉門道行軍大將，與突厥啟民可汗連兵擊伊吾。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shixiong was made campaigning general of the Yumen route and, joining forces with the Türk Qimin Khan, attacked Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Shixiong was made campaigning general of the Yumen route and, joining forces with the Türk Qimin Khan, attacked Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 師次玉門，啟民可汗背約，兵不至，世雄孤軍度磧。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yumen, Qimin Khan broke the agreement and his troops did not come; Shixiong crossed the desert with his lone army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yumen, Qimin Khan broke the agreement and his troops never came; Shixiong crossed the desert with his lone army.

sentences.zh: 伊吾初謂隋軍不能至，皆不設備，及聞世雄兵已度磧，大懼，請降，詣軍門上牛酒。

translations.literal: Yiwu at first believed Sui troops could not arrive and made no preparations; when they heard Shixiong's army had already crossed the desert they were greatly afraid, submitted, and came to the camp gate offering cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu at first believed Sui troops could not reach them and made no preparations; when they heard that Shixiong's army had already crossed the desert they were greatly afraid, submitted, and came to the camp gate with cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 世雄遂于漢舊伊吾城東築城，號新伊吾，留銀青光祿大夫王威以甲卒千餘人戍之而還。

translations.literal: Shixiong then built a city east of the old Han city of Yiwu, naming it New Yiwu; he left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal Wang Wei with more than a thousand armored soldiers to garrison it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong then built a city east of the old Han city of Yiwu, naming it New Yiwu; he left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal Wang Wei with more than a thousand armored soldiers to garrison it and returned.

sentences.zh: 天子大悅，進位正議大夫，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and promoted him to Master for Regular Remonstrance, granting two thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased, promoted him to Master for Regular Remonstrance, and granted two thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以世雄為沃沮道軍將，與宇文述同敗績於平壤。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was made army commander of the Woju route and, together with Yuwen Shu, suffered defeat at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was made army commander of the Woju route and, together with Yuwen Shu, suffered defeat at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 還次白石山，為賊所圍百餘重，四面矢下如雨。

translations.literal: On the return they halted at Baishi Mountain and were surrounded by bandits in more than a hundred rings; arrows fell from all four sides like rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the return they halted at Baishi Mountain and were surrounded by bandits in more than a hundred rings; arrows fell from every side like rain.

sentences.zh: 世雄以羸師為方陣，選勁騎二百先犯之，賊稍卻，因而縱擊，遂破之而還。

translations.literal: Shixiong arrayed his weakened troops in a square formation, selected two hundred crack horsemen to strike first at the enemy; the bandits fell back slightly, and he then unleashed a full attack, broke through, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong arrayed his weakened troops in a square formation and selected two hundred crack horsemen to strike first; the bandits fell back slightly, and he then unleashed a full attack, broke through, and returned.

sentences.zh: 所亡失多，竟坐免。

translations.literal: Losses were heavy, and in the end he was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Losses were heavy, and in the end he was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征遼東，拜右候衛將軍，兵指蹋頓道。

translations.literal: The following year the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong and appointed him General of the Right Rear Guard; his troops marched by the Tadun route.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong and appointed him General of the Right Rear Guard; his troops marched by the Tadun route.

sentences.zh: 軍至烏骨城，會楊玄感作亂，班師。

translations.literal: When the army reached Wugu city, it happened that Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, and they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Wugu city, Yang Xuangan rebelled, and the forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝至柳城，以世雄為東北道大使，行燕郡太守，鎮懷遠。

translations.literal: The emperor reached Liucheng and appointed Shixiong envoy of the Northeast Route, acting Administrator of Yan commandery, to garrison Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Liucheng, he appointed Shixiong envoy of the Northeast Route and acting Administrator of Yan commandery, garrisoning Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 于時突厥頗為寇盜，緣邊諸郡多苦之，詔世雄發十二郡士馬，巡塞而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Türks frequently raided and plundered, and the commanderies along the frontier suffered greatly; an edict ordered Shixiong to mobilize troops and horses from twelve commanderies, patrol the frontier passes, and return.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Türks raided frequently, and the frontier commanderies suffered greatly; an edict ordered Shixiong to mobilize troops from twelve commanderies, patrol the border passes, and return.

sentences.zh: 十年，復從帝至遼東，遷左禦衛大將軍，仍領涿郡留守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again followed the emperor to Liaodong, was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Courage Guard, and still held the post of garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again followed the emperor to Liaodong, was made General-in-Chief of the Left Courage Guard, and continued as garrison commander of Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密逼東都，中原騷動，詔世雄率幽、薊精兵將擊之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi pressed upon the Eastern Capital, the Central Plain was in turmoil, and an edict ordered Shixiong to lead elite troops from You and Ji to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Mi pressed upon the Eastern Capital and the Central Plain was in turmoil; an edict ordered Shixiong to lead elite troops from You and Ji to attack him.

sentences.zh: 軍次河間，營于郡城南，河間諸縣並集兵，依世雄大軍為營，欲討竇建德。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hejian and encamped south of the commandery city; all the counties of Hejian gathered troops and, relying on Shixiong's great army for their camp, intended to punish Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Hejian and encamped south of the commandery seat; the counties of Hejian all gathered troops and pitched camp around Shixiong's main force, intending to attack Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德將家口遁，自選精銳數百，夜來襲之。

translations.literal: Jiande fled with his household, himself selected several hundred crack troops, and came by night to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande fled with his family, personally selected several hundred crack troops, and raided them by night.

sentences.zh: 先犯河間兵，潰奔世雄營。

translations.literal: They first struck the Hejian troops, who routed and fled into Shixiong's camp.
translations.idiomatic: They first struck the Hejian troops, who broke and fled into Shixiong's camp.

sentences.zh: 時遇雰霧晦冥，莫相辨識，軍不得成列，皆騰柵而走，於是大敗。

translations.literal: At the time they encountered thick fog and darkness; none could tell friend from foe, the army could not form ranks, and all leaped the palisades and fled—thereupon came a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Thick fog descended and none could tell friend from foe; the army could not hold its ranks, men leaped the palisades and fled, and the force was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 世雄與左右數十騎遁入河間城，慚恚發病，歸於涿郡，未幾而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Shixiong fled with several dozen horsemen of his personal suite into Hejian city; shame and rage brought on illness, he returned to Zhuo commandery, and before long died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong fled into Hejian city with several dozen horsemen of his personal suite; consumed by shame and rage he fell ill, returned to Zhuo commandery, and died soon afterward at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 有子萬述、萬淑、萬鈞、萬徹，並以驍武知名。

translations.literal: He had sons Wanshu, Wanshu, Wanjun, and Wanche—all renowned for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons—Wanshu, Wanshu, Wanjun, and Wanche—all renowned for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 王仁恭

translations.literal: Wang Rengong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengong

sentences.zh: 王仁恭，字元實，天水上邽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rengong, styled Yuanshi, was a native of Shanggui in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengong, styled Yuanshi, came from Shanggui in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖建，周鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was Prefect of Fengzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had been Prefect of Fengzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父猛，鄯州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Meng was Prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng had been Prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁恭少剛毅修謹，工騎射。

translations.literal: Rengong in youth was firm, resolute, and careful in conduct, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rengong was firm, disciplined, and careful, and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州補主簿，秦孝王引為記室，轉長道令，遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: At age twenty he was appointed chief clerk by the prefecture; Prince Xiao of Qin brought him in as registrar, then he was transferred to magistrate of Changdao and promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was made chief clerk of the prefecture; Prince Xiao of Qin took him on as registrar, after which he became magistrate of Changdao and was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從楊素擊突厥于靈武，以功拜上開府，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: He followed Yang Su in attacking the Türks at Lingwu; for merit he was appointed Upper Opener of the Government and granted three thousand bundles of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yang Su in attacking the Türks at Lingwu; for his merit he was made Upper Opener of the Government and granted three thousand bundles of goods.

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍典蜀王軍事。

translations.literal: As General of Swift Cavalry he managed the military affairs of the Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As General of Swift Cavalry he directed the military affairs of the Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 山獠作亂，蜀王命仁恭討破之，賜奴婢三百口。

translations.literal: The mountain Liao rebelled; the Prince of Shu ordered Rengong to suppress and defeat them, and he was granted three hundred male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: When the mountain Liao rebelled, the Prince of Shu ordered Rengong to put them down; for defeating them he was granted three hundred servants.

sentences.zh: 及蜀王以罪廢，官屬多罹其患。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu was deposed for crime, many of his officials suffered calamity on his account.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu was deposed for crime, many of his staff were caught up in the fallout.

sentences.zh: 上以仁恭素質直，置而不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Rengong had always been straightforward by nature, set the matter aside and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rengong had always been straightforward, the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒舉兵反，從楊素擊平之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion; Rengong followed Yang Su to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, Prince of Han Liang rebelled; Rengong followed Yang Su and helped put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 以功進位大將軍，拜呂州刺史，賜帛四千匹，女妓十人。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Great General, appointed Prefect of Lüzhou, and granted four thousand bolts of silk and ten female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Great General, made Prefect of Lüzhou, and granted four thousand bolts of silk and ten female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉衛州刺史，尋改為汲郡太守，有能名。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Prefect of Weizhou; soon he was changed to Administrator of Ji commandery and gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to Prefect of Weizhou, then made Administrator of Ji commandery, where he won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 征入朝，帝呼上殿，勞勉之，賜雜彩六百段，良馬二匹。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, the emperor called him up to the hall, consoled and encouraged him, and granted six hundred bundles of mixed silks and two fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, the emperor had him called up to the hall, praised and encouraged him, and granted six hundred bundles of mixed silks and two fine horses.

sentences.zh: 遷信都太守，汲郡吏民扣馬號哭於道，數日不得出境，其得人情如此。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Xindu; the officials and people of Ji commandery seized his horse's bridle and wept on the road, and for several days he could not leave the border—such was the affection he had won.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Administrator of Xindu, the officials and people of Ji commandery seized his horse's bridle and wept in the road; for days he could not leave the commandery—such was the affection he had won.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以仁恭為軍將。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was made an army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he served as an army commander.

sentences.zh: 及帝班師，仁恭為殿，遇賊，擊走之。

translations.literal: When the emperor withdrew the army, Rengong served as rearguard; encountering bandits, he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew, Rengong commanded the rearguard; he met bandits, attacked them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 進授左光祿大夫，賜絹六千段，馬四十匹。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted six thousand bolts of silk and forty horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted six thousand bolts of silk and forty horses.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以軍將指扶餘道，帝謂之曰：「往者諸軍多不利，公獨以一軍破賊。

translations.literal: The following year he again served as army commander toward the Fuyu route; the emperor said to him, "In the past many armies fared badly, yet you alone with one army broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as army commander on the Fuyu route; the emperor said to him, "In the past many armies fared badly, yet you alone with one army broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 古人云，敗軍之將不可以言勇，諸將其可任乎？

translations.literal: The ancients said that a general of a defeated army may not speak of courage—can the other generals be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that a defeated general may not speak of courage—can the other commanders really be trusted?

sentences.zh: 今委公為前軍，當副所望也。

translations.literal: Now I entrust you as vanguard—you should meet what is hoped of you.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am entrusting you with the vanguard; you must live up to what I expect.

sentences.zh: 」賜良馬十匹，黃金百兩。

translations.literal: " He was granted ten fine horses and a hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he was granted ten fine horses and a hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遂進軍，至新城，賊數萬背城結陣，仁恭率勁騎一千擊破之。

translations.literal: Rengong then advanced; reaching Xincheng, several tens of thousands of bandits formed battle lines with their backs to the city; Rengong led a thousand crack horsemen and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong then advanced to Xincheng, where tens of thousands of bandits formed battle lines with their backs to the city wall; he led a thousand crack horsemen and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊嬰城拒守，仁恭四面攻圍。

translations.literal: The bandits clung to the city and resisted; Rengong attacked and besieged from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits held the city and resisted; Rengong besieged it on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大悅，遣舍人詣軍勞問，賜以珍物。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly pleased; he sent a palace secretary to the army to console and inquire, granting precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased when he heard, sent a palace secretary to the army with greetings, and granted precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 進授光祿大夫，賜絹五千匹。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted five thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and granted five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，其兄子武賁郎將仲伯預焉，仁恭由是坐免。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, his elder brother's son Colonel of the Martial Retainers Zhongbo took part; Rengong on that account was dismissed and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, his nephew Colonel of the Martial Retainers Zhongbo took part; Rengong was dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 尋而突厥屢為寇患，帝以仁恭宿將，頻有戰功，詔復本官，領馬邑太守。

translations.literal: Before long the Türks repeatedly raided; because Rengong was a veteran general with repeated battle merits, an edict restored him to his former office and made him Administrator of Mayi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Türks raided repeatedly; because Rengong was a veteran with many victories, an edict restored his former office and made him Administrator of Mayi commandery.

sentences.zh: 其年，始畢可汗率騎數萬來寇馬邑，復令二特勤將兵南過。

translations.literal: That year Shibi Khan led several tens of thousands of horsemen to raid Mayi and again sent two tegins to lead troops southward across the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shibi Khan led tens of thousands of horsemen against Mayi and sent two tegins to lead troops south across the border.

sentences.zh: 時郡兵不滿三千，仁恭簡精銳逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery troops numbered fewer than three thousand; Rengong selected crack troops to meet the attack head-on and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had fewer than three thousand troops; Rengong selected crack troops, met the enemy head-on, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 其二特勤眾亦潰，仁恭縱兵乘之，獲數千級，並斬二特勤。

translations.literal: The forces of the two tegins also routed; Rengong unleashed his troops to pursue, taking several thousand heads and beheading both tegins.
translations.idiomatic: The two tegins' forces also broke; Rengong pursued with all his troops, took several thousand heads, and beheaded both tegins.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜縑三千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted three thousand bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted three thousand bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥復入定襄，仁恭率兵四千掩擊，斬千餘級，大獲六畜而歸。

translations.literal: Afterward the Türks again entered Dingxiang; Rengong led four thousand troops in a surprise attack, beheaded more than a thousand, and returned with a great haul of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Türks again entered Dingxiang; Rengong led four thousand men in a surprise attack, took more than a thousand heads, and returned with a great haul of livestock.

sentences.zh: 于時天下大亂，百姓饑餒，道路隔絕，仁恭頗改舊節，受納貨賄，又不敢輒開倉廩，賑恤百姓。

translations.literal: At that time the empire was in great disorder, the people were hungry and starving, and roads were cut off; Rengong greatly changed his former conduct, accepting bribes, yet he still did not dare readily open the granaries to relieve and succor the people.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was in turmoil, the people were starving, and roads were cut off; Rengong departed from his former integrity, accepting bribes, yet still did not dare open the granaries to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 其麾下校尉劉武周與仁恭侍婢奸通，恐事泄，將為亂，每宣言郡中曰：「父老妻子凍餒，填委溝壑，而王府君閉倉不救百姓，是何理也！

translations.literal: A commandant under him, Liu Wuzhou, committed adultery with one of Rengong's serving maids; fearing exposure, he intended to raise rebellion and repeatedly proclaimed throughout the commandery, "Fathers, elders, wives, and children freeze and starve, filling ditches and gullies, yet Prefect Wang keeps the granaries closed and will not save the people—what principle is this!
translations.idiomatic: A commandant under him, Liu Wuzhou, had an affair with one of Rengong's serving maids; fearing exposure, he plotted rebellion and repeatedly proclaimed throughout the commandery, "Fathers, elders, wives, and children freeze and starve, filling ditches and gullies, yet Prefect Wang keeps the granaries closed and will not save the people—what sort of justice is that!

sentences.zh: 」以此激怒眾，吏民頗怨之。

translations.literal: " With this he inflamed the masses, and officials and people grew greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: " With this he inflamed the people, and officials and commoners grew deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 其後仁恭正坐聽事，武周率其徒數十人大呼而入，因害之，時年六十。

translations.literal: Afterward, as Rengong sat in audience conducting affairs, Wuzhou led several dozen of his followers shouting as they entered, and thereby killed him; he was sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Rengong was presiding in the hall of audience, Wuzhou led several dozen followers bursting in with a shout and killed him; he was sixty years old.

sentences.zh: 武周於是開倉賑給，郡內皆從之，自稱天子，署置百官，轉攻傍郡。

translations.literal: Wuzhou thereupon opened the granaries to distribute relief; all within the commandery followed him; he styled himself Son of Heaven, appointed a full set of officials, and turned to attack neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou then opened the granaries and distributed grain; the whole commandery rallied to him. He styled himself emperor, appointed officials, and began attacking neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 權武，字武挵，天水人也。

translations.literal: Quan Wu, styled Wunong, was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wu, styled Wunong, came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖超，魏秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chao was Prefect of Qinzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chao had been Prefect of Qinzhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父襲慶，周開府，從武元皇帝與齊師戰於并州，被圍百餘重。

translations.literal: His father Xiqing was an Opener of the Government under Zhou; he followed Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou against the Qi army at Bingzhou and was surrounded in more than a hundred rings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiqing held the rank of Opener of the Government under the Zhou; he followed Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou against the Qi at Bingzhou and was encircled in more than a hundred rings.

sentences.zh: 襲慶力戰矢盡，短兵接戰，殺傷甚眾，刀矛皆折，脫胄擲地，向賊大罵曰：「何不來斫頭也！

translations.literal: Xiqing fought fiercely until his arrows were exhausted, then fought hand to hand at close quarters, killing and wounding many; sabers and spears all broke; he removed his helmet and cast it to the ground, and shouted at the enemy, "Why do you not come and chop off my head!
translations.idiomatic: Xiqing fought until his arrows were spent, then closed to hand-to-hand combat, killing and wounding many; when sabers and spears broke he cast off his helmet, threw it to the ground, and shouted at the enemy, "Why don't you come and take my head!

sentences.zh: 」賊遂殺之。

translations.literal: " The enemy thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy then killed him.

sentences.zh: 武以忠臣子，起家拜開府，襲爵齊郡公，邑千二百戶。

translations.literal: Wu, as the son of a loyal minister, began his career appointed Opener of the Government, inheriting the title Duke of Qi commandery with a fief of one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a loyal minister, Wu began his career as Opener of the Government, inheriting the title Duke of Qi commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 武少果勁，勇力絕人，能重甲上馬。

translations.literal: Wu in youth was resolute and bold, his courage and strength surpassing other men; he could mount a horse while wearing heavy armor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wu was resolute and bold, with strength beyond ordinary men; he could mount a horse while wearing heavy armor.

sentences.zh: 嘗倒投于井，未及泉，復躍而出，其拳捷如此。

translations.literal: Once he was thrown headfirst into a well; before reaching the water he leaped out again—such was his agility in combat.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was thrown headfirst into a well; before he reached the water he leaped out again—such was his astonishing agility.

sentences.zh: 從王謙破齊服龍等五城，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Qian in capturing five cities including Fulong of Qi, and his fief was increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Qian in capturing five Qi cities including Fulong, and his fief was increased by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，攻陷邵州，別下六城，以功增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Qi he stormed and took Shaozhou and separately captured six cities; for merit his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to pacify Qi he took Shaozhou and captured six other cities; for his merit his fief was increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，拜勁捷左旅上大夫，進位上開府。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was appointed Senior Grand Master of the Left Swift Brigade and advanced to Upper Opener of the Government.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was made Senior Grand Master of the Left Swift Brigade and promoted to Upper Opener of the Government.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，引置左右。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, he brought Wu in and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chief minister, he brought Wu into his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Wu's fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne, Wu's fief was increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後六歲，拜淅州刺史。

translations.literal: Six years later he was appointed Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was made Prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以行軍總管從晉王出六合，還拜豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he served as Mobile Campaign Commander under Prince Jin, marching out from Liuhe; on his return he was appointed Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he served as mobile campaign commander under Prince Jin, marching from Liuhe; on his return he was made Prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，以創業之舊，進位大將軍，檢校潭州總管。

translations.literal: After several years in office, as one who had shared in the founding, he was advanced to Great General and made acting regional commander of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, as one who had helped found the dynasty, he was promoted to Great General and made acting regional commander of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年，桂州人李世賢作亂，武以行軍總管與武候大將軍虞慶則擊平之。

translations.literal: That year Li Shixian of Guizhou raised rebellion; Wu, as mobile campaign commander, together with Great General of the Martial Guards Yu Qingze, attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Shixian of Guizhou rebelled; Wu, as mobile campaign commander, joined Great General of the Martial Guards Yu Qingze in putting down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 慶則以罪誅，功竟不錄，復還於州。

translations.literal: Qingze was executed for crime, and Wu's merit was in the end not recorded; he returned again to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qingze was executed for a crime, and Wu's achievement went unrewarded; he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 多造金帶，遺嶺南酋領，其人復答以寶物，武皆納之，由是致富。

translations.literal: He had many gold belts made and sent them as gifts to chieftains of Lingnan; they in turn replied with precious objects, all of which Wu accepted—thereby he grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: He had many gold belts made and sent them to Lingnan chieftains, who repaid him with precious goods; Wu accepted them all and grew wealthy.

sentences.zh: 後武晚生一子，與親客宴集，酒酣，遂擅赦所部內獄囚。

translations.literal: Later Wu in his old age fathered a son; with intimate guests at a feast, when the wine had gone deep, he thereupon on his own authority pardoned the prisoners in the jails within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu fathered a son in his old age, he held a feast with close friends; deep in his cups he pardoned the prisoners in his jurisdiction on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 武常以南越邊遠，治從其俗，務適便宜，不依律令，而每言當今法急，官不可為。

translations.literal: Wu often said that because the Southern Yue frontier was remote, government should follow local custom and seek what was convenient, not obey statutes—and he frequently remarked that the laws of the day were harsh and office could not be borne.
translations.idiomatic: Wu often held that because the Southern Yue frontier was remote, rule should follow local custom and practicality rather than statute; he also remarked constantly that the laws were too harsh and official life was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 上令有司案其事，皆驗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate the matter; all was verified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an investigation; every charge was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 武於獄中上書，言其父為武元皇帝戰死于馬前，以此求哀。

translations.literal: Wu from prison submitted a memorial saying his father had died fighting before the horse of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, and on that account sought mercy.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Wu submitted a memorial saying his father had died fighting before Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou's horse, and pleaded for mercy on that account.

sentences.zh: 由是除名為民。

translations.literal: On that account he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，復拜大將軍，封邑如舊。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was again appointed Great General, his fief restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was again made Great General with his fief restored as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜右武衛大將軍，坐事免，授桂州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded he was appointed Great General of the Right Martial Guard; for an offense he was dismissed and made Prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wu was made Great General of the Right Martial Guard; dismissed for an offense, he was appointed Prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄轉始安太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Administrator of Shian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Administrator of Shian commandery.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵拜右屯衛大將軍，尋坐事除名。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Great General of the Right Garrison Guard; soon he was dismissed and stripped of name for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After a long absence from court he was summoned and made Great General of the Right Garrison Guard; soon he was dismissed and disgraced for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 有子弘。

translations.literal: He had a son Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Hong.

sentences.zh: 吐萬緒

translations.literal: Tu Wanxu
translations.idiomatic: Tu Wanxu

sentences.zh: 吐萬緒，字長緒，代郡鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Tu Wanxu, styled Changxu, was a native of the Xianbei of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Wanxu, styled Changxu, was of Xianbei descent from Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父通，周郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tong was Prefect of Yingzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong had been Prefect of Yingzhou under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 緒少有武略，在周，起家撫軍將軍，襲爵元壽縣公。

translations.literal: Xu from youth had military talent and strategy; under Zhou he began his career as Pacification General, inheriting the title Duke of Yuanshou county.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xu showed military talent; under the Zhou he began his career as Pacification General and inherited the title Duke of Yuanshou county.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，累遷大將軍、少司武。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns; he was promoted step by step to Great General and Junior Director of Martial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns and rose step by step to Great General and Junior Director of Martial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜襄州總管，進封穀城郡公，邑二千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Xu was appointed regional commander of Xiangzhou, advanced to Duke of Gucheng commandery with a fief of two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne, Xu was made regional commander of Xiangzhou and advanced to Duke of Gucheng commandery with a fief of twenty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋轉青州總管，頗有治名。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Qingzhou and gained a considerable reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Qingzhou, where he earned a solid reputation for governance.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，突厥寇邊，朝廷以緒有威略，徙為朔州總管，甚為北夷所憚。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Türks raided the frontier; the court, because Xu had prestige and strategy, moved him to regional commander of Shuozhou, and the northern barbarians greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After a year the Türks raided the frontier; the court moved Xu to regional commander of Shuozhou on account of his prestige and ability, and the northern peoples greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 其後高祖潛有吞陳之志，轉徐州總管，令修戰具。

translations.literal: Afterward Gaozu secretly harbored the ambition to swallow Chen; Xu was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and ordered to prepare weapons of war.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gaozu secretly planned the conquest of Chen, Xu was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and ordered to prepare arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 及大舉濟江，以緒領行軍總管，與西河公紇豆陵、洪景屯兵江北。

translations.literal: When the great force crossed the Yangzi, Xu served as mobile campaign commander and, together with Duke of Xihe Gedouling and Hong Jing, encamped troops on the north bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force crossed the Yangzi, Xu served as mobile campaign commander and, with Duke of Xihe Gedouling and Hong Jing, encamped on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，拜夏州總管。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was appointed regional commander of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified, he was made regional commander of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣之在籓也，頗見親遇，及為太子，引為左虞候率。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang was at his princely establishment he was greatly favored; when Guang became heir apparent, he brought Xu in as Left Commandant of the Household Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang held his fief he enjoyed great favor; when Guang became heir apparent he made Xu Left Commandant of the Household Guards.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒時鎮并州，帝恐其為變，拜緒晉、絳二州刺史，馳傳之官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, Prince of Han Liang was then garrisoning Bingzhou; the emperor feared he would change allegiance, appointed Xu Prefect of the two prefectures Jin and Jiang, and sent him post-haste to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, Prince of Han Liang held Bingzhou; fearing trouble, the emperor appointed Xu Prefect of Jin and Jiang and sent him post-haste to take office.

sentences.zh: 緒未出關，諒已遣兵據蒲阪，斷河橋，緒不得進。

translations.literal: Before Xu had left the pass, Liang had already sent troops to seize Puban, cut the river bridge, and Xu could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xu had left the pass, Liang had already sent troops to seize Puban and destroy the river bridge, blocking Xu's advance.

sentences.zh: 詔緒率兵從楊素擊破之，拜左武候將軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xu to lead troops, follow Yang Su, and defeat him; he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xu to follow Yang Su and defeat the rebels; he was then made General of the Left Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉光祿卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Director of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era he was made Director of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼之遇讒也，引緒為證，緒明其無罪，由是免官。

translations.literal: When Heruo Bi was slandered, he brought Xu in as witness; Xu showed he was without guilt, and on that account Xu was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Heruo Bi fell victim to slander, he called Xu as witness; Xu testified to his innocence, and for that Xu lost his office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，守東平太守。

translations.literal: After more than a year he served as Administrator of Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he served as Administrator of Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝幸江都，路經其境，迎謁道傍。

translations.literal: Before long, the emperor visited Jiangdu; the route passed through his jurisdiction, and he received and paid homage beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor visited Jiangdu; as the route passed through Xu's territory, Xu received him and paid homage beside the road.

sentences.zh: 帝命升龍舟，緒因頓首陳謝往事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to board the imperial dragon boat; Xu thereupon kowtowed and pleaded apology for past affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him aboard the imperial dragon boat; Xu kowtowed and apologized for what had passed.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，拜金紫光祿大夫，太守如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, enfeoffed him Grand Master of Golden Chariots with Purple Trappings, and kept him as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, made him Grand Master of Golden Chariots with Purple Trappings, and left him in office as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，請為先鋒，帝嘉之，拜左屯衛大將軍，率馬步數萬指蓋馬道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he asked to serve as vanguard; the emperor praised this, appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard, and led tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry toward the Gaima route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he volunteered as vanguard; the emperor praised him, appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard, and he led tens of thousands of horse and foot toward the Gaima route.

sentences.zh: 及班師，留鎮懷遠，進位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was left to garrison Huaiyuan and was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, he was left to garrison Huaiyuan and was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時劉元進作亂江南，以兵攻潤州，帝征緒討之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yuanjin raised rebellion in Jiangnan and sent troops to attack Runzhou; the emperor summoned Xu to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yuanjin rebelled in Jiangnan and attacked Runzhou with troops; the emperor summoned Xu to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 緒率眾至楊子津，元進自茅浦將渡江，緒勒兵擊走。

translations.literal: Xu led his force to Yangzi Ford; Yuanjin was about to cross the river from Maopu; Xu marshaled his troops and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xu led his troops to Yangzi Ford; Yuanjin was about to cross from Maopu; Xu marshaled his force and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 緒因濟江，背水為柵。

translations.literal: Xu then crossed the river and made a palisade with the water at his back.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then crossed the river and built a palisade with the water at his back.

sentences.zh: 明旦，元進來攻，又大挫之，賊解潤州圍而去。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Yuanjin came to attack and Xu again routed him; the rebels lifted the siege of Runzhou and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Yuanjin attacked and Xu routed him again; the rebels lifted the siege of Runzhou and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 緒進屯曲阿，元進復結柵拒。

translations.literal: Xu advanced and encamped at Qu'e; Yuanjin again built palisades to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Xu advanced and encamped at Qu'e; Yuanjin again built palisades to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 緒挑之，元進出戰，陣未整，緒以騎突之，賊眾遂潰，赴江水而死者數萬。

translations.literal: Xu provoked him; Yuanjin came out to fight; before his formation was set, Xu broke in with cavalry; the rebel masses routed, and tens of thousands died rushing into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xu provoked him into battle; Yuanjin came out to fight, but before his lines were set Xu charged with cavalry; the rebel host broke, and tens of thousands drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 元進挺身夜遁，歸保其壘。

translations.literal: Yuanjin slipped away alone by night and returned to hold his fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin slipped away alone by night and returned to hold his camp.

sentences.zh: 偽署僕射硃燮、管崇等屯於毗陵，連營百餘里。

translations.literal: The falsely appointed Vice Director Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others were encamped at Piling, their linked camps stretching more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Vice Director Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others were encamped at Piling in linked camps stretching more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 緒乘勢進擊，復破之，賊退保黃山。

translations.literal: Xu pressed the advantage and attacked again, defeating them once more; the rebels withdrew to hold Huangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu pressed the attack and routed them again; the rebels withdrew to hold Huangshan.

sentences.zh: 緒進軍圍之，賊窮蹙請降，元進、硃燮僅以身免。

translations.literal: Xu advanced and besieged them; the rebels, pressed to extremity, begged to surrender; Yuanjin and Zhu Xie barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xu advanced and besieged them; the rebels, driven to extremity, begged to surrender; Yuanjin and Zhu Xie barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 于陣斬管崇及其將軍陸顗等五千餘人，收其子女三萬餘口，送江都宮。

translations.literal: On the field he beheaded Guan Chong and his general Lu Yi and more than five thousand others, took more than thirty thousand wives and children captive, and sent them to the Jiangdu palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the battlefield he beheaded Guan Chong and his general Lu Yi and more than five thousand others, took more than thirty thousand women and children captive, and sent them to the Jiangdu palace.

sentences.zh: 進解會稽圍。

translations.literal: He went on to lift the siege of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He then went on to lift the siege of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 元進復據建安，帝令進討之，緒以士卒疲敝，請息甲待至來春。

translations.literal: Yuanjin again seized Jian'an; the emperor ordered Xu to advance and suppress him; Xu, because the soldiers were worn out, asked to rest the army and wait until the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin again held Jian'an; the emperor ordered Xu to advance and suppress him, but Xu, finding his troops exhausted, asked to stand down and wait until spring.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，密令求緒罪失，有司奏緒怯懦違詔，於是除名為民，配防建安。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, secretly ordered a search for Xu's faults; the relevant offices memorialized that Xu was cowardly and disobeyed the edict; thereupon he was stripped of rank and made a commoner, assigned to garrison duty at Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and secretly ordered a search for Xu's faults; the relevant offices memorialized that Xu was cowardly and had disobeyed the edict; he was then stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and assigned to garrison Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔征詣行在所，緒鬱鬱不得志，還至永嘉，發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Soon an edict summoned him to the emperor's traveling residence; Xu, depressed and without fulfillment, returned as far as Yongjia, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict summoned him to the emperor's traveling residence; Xu, depressed and unfulfilled, returned as far as Yongjia, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 董純，字德厚，隴西成紀人也。

translations.literal: Dong Chun, styled Dehou, was a native of Chengji in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chun, styled Dehou, was a native of Chengji in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖和，魏太子左衛率。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was Left Guard Commandant of the Heir Apparent under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He had been Left Guard Commandant of the Heir Apparent under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父升，周柱國。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was a Pillar of State under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had been a Pillar of State under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 純少有膂力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Chun from youth had physical strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chun had great physical strength and was skilled with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 在周仕歷司禦上士、典馭下大夫，封固始縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he served in succession as Senior Clerk of the Chariot Office and Junior Grandee of the Chariot Registry; he was enfeoffed Baron of Gushi county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served in succession as Senior Clerk of the Chariot Office and Junior Grandee of the Chariot Registry, and was enfeoffed Baron of Gushi county with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，以功拜儀同，進爵大興縣侯，增邑通前八百戶。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi; for merit he was appointed Commissioner with Equal Status, advanced to Marquis of Daxing county, and his fief was increased to eight hundred households together with what he had held before.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi; for merit he was appointed Commissioner with Equal Status, advanced to Marquis of Daxing county, and his fief was increased to eight hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵漢曲縣公，累遷驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Hanqu county and promoted in succession to General of Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Hanqu county and rose in succession to General of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功進位上開府。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was advanced to Senior Grandee of a Separate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was advanced to Senior Grandee of a Separate Office.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以勞舊擢拜左衛將軍，尋改封順政縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, on account of long service he was promoted and appointed General of the Left Guard; soon he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Shunzheng county.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era, on account of long service he was promoted to General of the Left Guard; soon he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Shunzheng county.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒作亂并州，以純為行軍總管、河北道安撫副使，從楊素擊平之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled in Bingzhou, Chun was made mobile campaign commander and deputy pacification commissioner of the Hebei route; he followed Yang Su and suppressed the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled in Bingzhou, Chun was made mobile campaign commander and deputy pacification commissioner on the Hebei route; he followed Yang Su and put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以功拜柱國，進爵為郡公，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Pillar of State, advanced to a commandery duke, and his fief was increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was appointed Pillar of State, advanced to commandery duke, and his fief was increased by two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉左備身將軍，賜女妓十人，縑彩五千匹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Attendant Guard and was granted ten female entertainers and five thousand bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Left Attendant Guard and granted ten female entertainers and five thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 數年，轉左驍衛將軍、彭城留守。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Left Valiant Guard and made garrison commander of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Left Valiant Guard and made garrison commander of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕之得罪也，純坐與交通，帝庭譴之曰：「汝階緣宿衛，以至大官，何乃附傍吾兒，欲相離間也？

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Yang was found guilty, Chun was implicated for associating with him; the emperor reprimanded him in court, saying: "You rose step by step through palace guard service to great office—why then attach yourself to my son and seek to drive us apart?
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Yang fell from favor, Chun was implicated for associating with him; the emperor reprimanded him in court, saying, "You rose through palace guard service to high office—why attach yourself to my son and seek to drive us apart?

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「臣本微賤下才，過蒙獎擢，先帝察臣小心，寵逾涯分，陛下重加收采，位至將軍。

translations.literal: Chun said: "Your servant was originally of humble origin and mediocre talent, yet was excessively favored and promoted; the former emperor saw my careful conduct and favored me beyond what I deserved; Your Majesty again showed me great regard, and I rose to the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Your servant was originally of humble origin and mediocre talent, yet was excessively favored and promoted; the former emperor saw my careful conduct and favored me beyond my deserts; Your Majesty again showed me great regard, and I rose to the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 欲竭餘年，報國恩耳。

translations.literal: I wish to exhaust what years remain to repay the state's grace, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to spend what years remain repaying the state's grace, that is all."

sentences.zh: 比數詣齊王者，徒以先帝、先後往在仁壽宮，置元德太子及齊王於膝上，謂臣曰：'汝好看此二兒，勿忘吾言也。

translations.literal: The reason I have lately visited the Prince of Qi so often is only that the former emperor and empress, when they were at Renshou Palace, set the Yuande Heir Apparent and the Prince of Qi on their knees and said to me: 'Look well after these two sons, and do not forget my words.'
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have lately visited the Prince of Qi so often is only that the former emperor and empress, when they were at Renshou Palace, set the Yuande Heir Apparent and the Prince of Qi on their knees and said to me, 'Look well after these two sons, and do not forget my words.'

sentences.zh: '臣奉詔之後，每於休暇出入，未嘗不詣王所。

translations.literal: After receiving that charge, whenever I went out in my days of rest I never failed to visit the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving that charge, whenever I went out on my days of rest I never failed to visit the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 臣誠不敢忘先帝之言。

translations.literal: Your servant truly dares not forget the former emperor's words.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly dares not forget the former emperor's words.

sentences.zh: 于時陛下亦侍先帝之側。

translations.literal: At that time Your Majesty also attended at the former emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Your Majesty also attended at the former emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 」帝改容曰：「誠有斯旨。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression and said: "There truly was such an intention."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed expression and said, "There truly was such an intention."

sentences.zh: 」於是舍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he released him.

sentences.zh: 後數日，出為汶山太守。

translations.literal: Several days later Chun was sent out as Administrator of Wenshan.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was sent out as Administrator of Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，突厥寇邊，朝廷以純宿將，轉為榆林太守。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Türks raided the frontier; the court, because Chun was a veteran general, transferred him to Administrator of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the Türks raided the frontier; the court, because Chun was a veteran general, transferred him to Administrator of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 虜有至境，純輒擊卻之。

translations.literal: Whenever the barbarians reached the border, Chun would strike and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the barbarians reached the border, Chun would strike and drive them back.

sentences.zh: 會彭城賊帥張大彪、宗世模等眾至數萬，保懸薄山，寇掠徐、兗。

translations.literal: Just then the bandit chiefs of Pengcheng Zhang Dabiao, Zong Shimou, and others, numbering in the tens of thousands, held Xuanbo Mountain and raided Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the bandit chiefs of Pengcheng, Zhang Dabiao and Zong Shimou, with forces numbering in the tens of thousands, held Xuanbo Mountain and raided Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 帝令純討之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chun to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 純初閉營不與戰，賊屢挑之不出，賊以純為怯，不設備，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: At first Chun closed his camp and would not fight; the bandits repeatedly provoked him but he would not come out; the bandits thought Chun was cowardly, took no precautions, and let their troops loot freely.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chun closed his camp and refused battle; the bandits repeatedly provoked him but he would not come out; thinking him cowardly, they took no precautions and let their troops loot freely.

sentences.zh: 純選精銳擊之，合戰於昌慮，大破之，斬首萬餘級，築為京觀。

translations.literal: Chun selected crack troops and struck; they joined battle at Changlü and he routed them completely, beheading more than ten thousand; he built a victory mound of severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: Chun selected crack troops and struck; they joined battle at Changlü and he routed them completely, beheading more than ten thousand; he built a victory mound from the severed heads.

sentences.zh: 賊魏騏驎眾萬餘人，據單父，純進擊，又破之。

translations.literal: The bandit Wei Qilin, with more than ten thousand followers, held Shanfu; Chun advanced and attacked and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Wei Qilin, with more than ten thousand followers, held Shanfu; Chun advanced, attacked, and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 及帝重征遼東，復以純為彭城留守。

translations.literal: When the emperor again launched the Liaodong campaign, Chun was again made garrison commander of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again launched the Liaodong campaign, Chun was again made garrison commander of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 東海賊彭孝才眾數千，掠懷仁縣，轉入沂水，保五不及山。

translations.literal: The bandit of Donghai Peng Xiaocai, with several thousand followers, plundered Huairen county, then moved into the Yi River region and held Wubuji Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Donghai bandit Peng Xiaocai, with several thousand followers, plundered Huairen county, then moved into the Yi River region and held Wubuji Mountain.

sentences.zh: 純以精兵擊之，擒孝才於陣，車裂之，餘黨各散。

translations.literal: Chun struck with elite troops, captured Xiaocai on the field, had him torn apart by chariots, and the remaining bandits scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Chun struck with elite troops, captured Xiaocai on the battlefield, had him torn apart by chariots, and the remaining bandits scattered.

sentences.zh: 時百姓思亂，盜賊日益，純雖頻戰克捷，所在蜂起。

translations.literal: At that time the common people longed for rebellion; bandits daily increased; though Chun won repeated victories in battle, uprisings swarmed everywhere he went.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people were ripe for rebellion; bandits grew daily; though Chun won repeated victories, uprisings swarmed wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 有人譖純怯懦，不能平賊，帝大怒，遣使鎖純詣東都。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Chun as cowardly and unable to pacify the bandits; the emperor was furious and sent envoys to chain Chun and bring him to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Chun as cowardly and unable to pacify the bandits; the emperor was furious and sent envoys to chain Chun and bring him to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 有司見帝怒甚，遂希旨致純死罪，竟伏誅。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, seeing the emperor's great anger, followed his intent and sentenced Chun to death; in the end he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices, seeing the emperor's great anger, followed his intent and sentenced Chun to death; in the end he was executed.

sentences.zh: 趙才，字孝才，張掖酒泉人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Cai, styled Xiaocai, was a native of Jiuquan in Zhangye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cai, styled Xiaocai, was a native of Jiuquan in Zhangye commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖隗，魏銀青光祿大夫、樂浪太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Trappings under Wei and Administrator of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui had been Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Trappings under Wei and Administrator of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 父壽，周順政太守。

translations.literal: His father Shou was Administrator of Shunzheng under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shou had been Administrator of Shunzheng under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 才少驍武，便弓馬，性粗悍，無威儀。

translations.literal: Cai from youth was fierce and martial, skilled with bow and horse; by nature he was rough and bold, without dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cai was fierce and martial, skilled with bow and horse; by nature he was rough and bold and lacked dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 周世為輿正上士。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou he served as Senior Clerk of the Chariot Master.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as Senior Clerk of the Chariot Master.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，屢以軍功遷上儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the throne, he was repeatedly promoted for military merit to Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank with Equal Status.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the throne, he was repeatedly promoted for military merit to Commissioner's Assistant of the Third Rank with Equal Status.

sentences.zh: 配事晉王，及王為太子，拜右虞候率。

translations.literal: He was assigned to serve Prince Jin; when the prince became heir apparent, Cai was appointed Right Commandant of the Household Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to serve Prince Jin; when the prince became heir apparent, Cai was appointed Right Commandant of the Household Guards.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉左備身驃騎，後遷右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, he was transferred to Charioteer General of the Left Attendant Guard, and later promoted to General of the Right Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded the throne, he was transferred to Charioteer General of the Left Attendant Guard, and later promoted to General of the Right Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝以才籓邸舊臣，漸見親待。

translations.literal: Because Cai was an old retainer from the prince's establishment, he was gradually favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cai was an old retainer from the prince's establishment, he gradually won favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 才亦恪勤匪懈，所在有聲。

translations.literal: Cai also was diligent without slackening and earned repute wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Cai also served diligently without slackening and earned repute wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉右候衛將軍。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to General of the Right Household Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to General of the Right Household Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，以為行軍總管，率衛尉卿劉權、兵部侍郎明雅等出合河道，與賊相遇，擊破之，以功進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Tuyuhun as mobile campaign commander, leading Minister Steward Liu Quan, Vice Minister of War Ming Ya, and others out through the Hehe route; they met the enemy and defeated them; for merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Golden Chariots with Purple Trappings.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Tuyuhun as mobile campaign commander, leading Minister Steward Liu Quan, Vice Minister of War Ming Ya, and others out by the Hehe route; they met the enemy and defeated them, and for merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Golden Chariots with Purple Trappings.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，再出碣石道，還授左候衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he again went out by the Jieshi route; on his return he was appointed General of the Left Household Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he again went out by the Jieshi route; on his return he was appointed General of the Left Household Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Household Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Household Guard.

sentences.zh: 時帝每有巡幸，才恆為斥候，肅遏奸非，無所回避。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Cai always served as advance scout, suppressing misconduct and wrongdoing, sparing no one.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Cai always served as advance scout, suppressing misconduct and wrongdoing without sparing anyone.

sentences.zh: 在途遇公卿妻子有違禁者，才輒醜言大罵。

translations.literal: On the road, if he met wives and children of high officials who violated prohibitions, Cai would revile them with foul language.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, if he met wives and children of high officials who violated prohibitions, Cai would revile them with foul language.

sentences.zh: 多所援及，時人雖患其不遜，然才守正，無如之何。

translations.literal: Many were implicated; though people resented his lack of deference, Cai held to rectitude and they could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Many were implicated; though people resented his lack of deference, Cai held to rectitude and they could do nothing about him.

sentences.zh: 十年駕幸汾陽宮，以才留守東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the imperial carriage visited Fenyang Palace; Cai was left to garrison the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the imperial carriage visited Fenyang Palace; Cai was left to garrison the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝在洛陽，將幸江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor was at Luoyang and planned to visit Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor was at Luoyang and planned to visit Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 才見四海土崩，恐為社稷之患，自以荷恩深重，無容坐看亡敗，於是入諫曰：「今百姓疲勞，府藏空竭，盜賊蜂起，禁令不行。

translations.literal: Cai saw the realm crumbling on every side and feared disaster for the state; feeling himself deeply bound by grace, he could not sit and watch ruin unfold; he therefore entered with remonstrance, saying: "Now the common people are exhausted, the treasury is empty, bandits swarm like bees, and prohibitions go unenforced.
translations.idiomatic: Cai saw the realm crumbling on every side and feared disaster for the state; feeling himself deeply bound by grace, he could not sit and watch ruin unfold; he therefore remonstrated, saying, "Now the people are exhausted, the treasury is empty, bandits swarm like bees, and prohibitions go unenforced.

sentences.zh: 願陛下還京師，安兆庶，臣雖愚蔽，敢以死請。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to return to the capital and settle the masses; though Your servant is dull and ignorant, I dare plead even unto death."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to return to the capital and settle the masses; though Your servant is dull and ignorant, I dare plead even unto death."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，以才屬吏。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and handed Cai over to the legal officers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and handed Cai over to the legal officers.

sentences.zh: 旬日，帝意頗解，乃令出之。

translations.literal: After ten days the emperor's mood eased somewhat, and he ordered Cai released.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days the emperor's mood eased somewhat, and he ordered Cai released.

sentences.zh: 帝遂幸江都，待遇逾昵。

translations.literal: The emperor then visited Jiangdu and treated Cai with even greater intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then visited Jiangdu and treated Cai with even greater intimacy.

sentences.zh: 時江都糧盡，將士離心，內史侍郎虞世基、秘書監袁充等多勸帝幸丹陽。
