translations.literal: At that time supplies at Jiangdu were exhausted and officers and soldiers were disheartened; Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, Director of the Palace Library Yuan Chong, and many others urged the emperor to visit Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time supplies at Jiangdu were exhausted and officers and soldiers were disheartened; Vice Director of the Secretariat Yu Shiji, Director of the Palace Library Yuan Chong, and many others urged the emperor to go to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝廷議其事，才極陳入京之策，世基盛言渡江之便。

translations.literal: The emperor held court to discuss the matter; Cai argued strongly for the policy of entering the capital; Shiji spoke at length of the convenience of crossing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court to discuss the matter; Cai argued strongly for returning to the capital; Shiji spoke at length of the convenience of crossing the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 帝默然無言，才與世基相忿而出。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent; Cai and Shiji left in mutual anger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent; Cai and Shiji left in mutual anger.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，才時在苑北，化及遣驍果席德方矯詔追之。

translations.literal: At the moment of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Cai was in the north of the park; Huaji sent the elite guard Xi Defang with a forged edict to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Cai was in the north of the park; Huaji sent the elite guard Xi Defang with a forged edict to summon him.

sentences.zh: 才聞詔而出，德方命其徒執之，以詣化及。

translations.literal: Cai heard the edict and came out; Defang ordered his men to seize him and bring him before Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Cai heard the edict and came out; Defang ordered his men to seize him and bring him before Huaji.

sentences.zh: 化及謂才曰：「今日之事，只得如此，幸勿為懷。

translations.literal: Huaji said to Cai: "Today's affair could only have turned out thus; please do not take it to heart."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji said to Cai, "Today's affair could only have turned out thus; please do not take it to heart."

sentences.zh: 」才默然不對。

translations.literal: Cai kept silent and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Cai kept silent and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 化及忿才無言，將殺之，三日乃釋。

translations.literal: Huaji, angered that Cai said nothing, was about to kill him, but after three days released him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, angered that Cai said nothing, was about to kill him, but after three days released him.

sentences.zh: 以本官從事，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: He continued in his original office, depressed and without fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: He continued in his original office, depressed and unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 才嘗對化及宴飲，請勸其同謀逆者一十八人楊士覽等酒，化及許之。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet with Huaji, Cai asked to propose a toast to the eighteen co-conspirators in the regicide, including Yang Shilan; Huaji consented.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet with Huaji, Cai asked to propose a toast to the eighteen co-conspirators in the regicide, including Yang Shilan; Huaji consented.

sentences.zh: 才執杯曰：「十八人止可一度作，勿復餘處更為。

translations.literal: Cai raised his cup and said: "Those eighteen men could only do this once; let there be no second such deed elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Cai raised his cup and said, "Those eighteen men could only do this once; let there be no second such deed elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」諸人默然不對。

translations.literal: All fell silent and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: All fell silent and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 行至聊城，遇疾。

translations.literal: When they reached Liaocheng, he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Liaocheng, he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及為竇建德所破，才復見虜。

translations.literal: Soon Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, and Cai was captured again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, and Cai was captured again.

sentences.zh: 心彌不平，數日而卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: His heart grew ever more unsettled; within several days he died, at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: His heart grew ever more unsettled; within several days he died, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 仁壽、大業間，有蘭興浴、賀蘭蕃，俱為武候將軍，剛嚴正直，不避強禦，咸以稱職知名。

translations.literal: Between the Renshou and Daye eras there were Lan Xingyu and Helan Fan, both Generals of the Martial Guards—stern, upright, and unafraid of the powerful; all were known for fulfilling their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Renshou and Daye eras there were Lan Xingyu and Helan Fan, both Generals of the Martial Guards—stern, upright, and unafraid of the powerful; both were known for fulfilling their duties.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：羅睺、法尚、李景、世雄、慕容三藏並以驍武之姿，當有事之日，致茲富貴，自取之也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Luohou, Fashang, Li Jing, Shixiong, and Murong Sancang all, with their fierce martial bearing, in days when service was needed attained such wealth and rank—they brought it on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Luohou, Fashang, Li Jing, Shixiong, and Murong Sancang all, with their fierce martial bearing, in days when service was needed attained such wealth and rank—they brought it on themselves.

sentences.zh: 仁恭初在汲郡，以清能顯達，後居馬邑，以貪吝敗亡，鮮克有終，惜矣！

translations.literal: Rengong at first in Jijun commandery rose to prominence through integrity and ability; later at Mayi he was ruined by greed and stinginess—few can keep a good end to the last; pity!
translations.idiomatic: Rengong at first in Jijun commandery rose to prominence through integrity and ability; later at Mayi he was ruined by greed and stinginess—few can keep a good end to the last; a pity!

sentences.zh: 吐萬緒、董純各以立效當年，取斯高秩。

translations.literal: Tu Wanxu and Dong Chun each, by establishing merit in their day, won such high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Wanxu and Dong Chun each, by establishing merit in their day, won such high rank.

sentences.zh: 緒請息兵見責，純遭譖毀被誅。

translations.literal: Xu, for asking to rest the army, was censured; Chun, slandered and ruined, was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, for asking to rest the army, was censured; Chun, slandered and ruined, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 大業之季，盜可盡乎！

translations.literal: In the Daye era, could bandits be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign, could the bandits ever be wiped out!

sentences.zh: 淫刑暴逞，能不及焉！

translations.literal: Licentious punishments ran rampant with violence—who could keep pace with that!
translations.idiomatic: Cruel punishments ran wild—who could match such excess!

sentences.zh: 趙才雖人而無儀，志在強直，固拒世基之議，可謂不苟同矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Cai, though human, lacked propriety; his intent was firm and upright; he firmly resisted Yu Shiji's proposals—one may call him not going along casually.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cai lacked the outward manners of a gentleman, yet his aim was forceful and straight; he steadfastly opposed Yu Shiji's schemes—a man who did not go along for convenience.

sentences.zh: 權武素無行檢，不拘刑憲，終取黜辱，宜哉。

translations.literal: Quan Wu from of old had no conduct or restraint, did not bind himself by penal statutes, and in the end received dismissal and disgrace—it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wu had long been without moral restraint and held himself above the penal code; that he ended in dismissal and disgrace was only as it should be.
